1.5 The Rust clair_fast Bitmask Engine (clair_fast/src/lib.rs)

To generate millions of exact dedP ground-truth bitmasks for Stage 1 organ pretraining and Stage 3 RLVR rewards without Python interpreter bottlenecks, Ember built clair_fast/src/lib.rs (796 lines of Rust + PyO3 + Rayon).

Every variable domain $a_i \subseteq \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ ($d \le 64$) is represented as a single u64 bitmask (Mask = u64), and every $r$-ary constraint tuple ($r \le 8$) is packed into a single u64 with 8 bits per slot (pack_tuple).

rust
pub type Mask = u64;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct TableCon {
    pub scope: Vec<usize>,
    pub tuples: Vec<u64>,           // packed: slot s in bits [8*s .. 8*s+8)
    pub sup: Vec<Vec<Mask>>,        // sup[s][v] = mask of allowed values, or per-tuple support
}

pub struct Csp {
    pub n: usize,
    pub d: usize,
    pub cons: Vec<TableCon>,
    pub by_var: Vec<Vec<usize>>,
}

The exact deduction operator exact_dedp_one uses a four-tier acceleration strategy:

  1. Bitwise GAC Pre-Pass (ac_fixpoint): Iterates support bitmasks until fixpoint; if any domain becomes 0, returns all-zeros immediately; if all domains become singletons (mask.count_ones() == 1), verifies and returns in $O(1)$ without search.
  2. Connected-Component & Free-Variable Stripping: Variables not touched by any constraint (by_var[i].is_empty()) keep their full mask a[i] untouched (out[i] = a[i]), avoiding a $d^{\text{free}}$ enumeration blowup.
  3. MRV Backtracking with Support Accumulation (solve_with_support): Explores the backtracking tree up to NODE_BUDGET = 2_000_000 nodes, OR-accumulating every complete solution sol into support[i] |= 1u64 << sol[i], and pruning values already known to be supported when checking remaining branches.
  4. Budget-Exceeded Fallback (dedp_per_value): If a dense graph exceeds NODE_BUDGET = 2_000_000 nodes during full solution enumeration, exact_dedp_one seamlessly switches to dedp_per_value, which runs a targeted decision SAT check (has_solution_with(csp, a, i, v)) only for the remaining (i, v) pairs not yet witnessed (support[i] & (1 << v) == 0).

Across 13,590 randomized CSP comparisons against the reference Python solver (test_clair_fast), clair_fast achieved 0 bitmask mismatches and a 29× to 56× wall-clock speedup on CPU via Rayon par_iter().

Part II: leanuweave & minidregg Projection — Verified Concurrent Document Weaving & Seam Synthesis

2.1 Architecture, Trust Floor & Scale (git@github.com:emberian/lean-uwueave.git)

In /Users/ember/dev/leanuweave (166 commits by Ember, README.md, docs/MAP.md), Ember constructed a 185-module, zero-Mathlib Lean 4 formalization and companion 177-test Rust engine for concurrent operational weaving, clash-graph seam coloring, multi-currency schedule synthesis, and bounded finite-product admission control.

The Mechanized Trust Gate (Uwueave/TrustFloor.lean & Uwueave/ExecRefine.lean)

Unlike formalizations that rely on external libraries or unchecked tactics, leanuweave enforces a compile-time metaprogramming audit in Uwueave/TrustFloor.lean over all 25,747 constants in the Uwueave.* namespace:

  • Zero sorryAx: Every theorem is constructively or classically closed.
  • Zero Lean.ofReduceBool / Lean.trustCompiler: native_decide is completely banned so the C++ compiler/evaluator is excluded from the trusted computing base.
  • Three Standard Axioms Only:
lean
  def allowedAxioms : List Name :=
    [``propext, ``Classical.choice, ``Quot.sound]

All computational synthesis procedures (greedySeamFor, synthesizeMinimumSeam, selectLeast, QuotaCheck, CatalogAdmission) are verified via the reflection bridge in Uwueave/ExecRefine.lean:

lean
theorem decide_sound (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (h : decide P = true) : P :=
  of_decide_eq_true h

theorem decide_complete (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (h : P) : decide P = true :=
  decide_eq_true h

theorem find?_sound {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) {x : α}
    (h : xs.find? p = some x) : x ∈ xs ∧ p x = true

theorem find?_complete_none {α : Type u} (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α)
    (h : xs.find? p = none) : ∀ x ∈ xs, p x = false

2.2 Semilattice Merge, I-Confluence & Seam Algebra (Uwueave/Confluence.lean, Uwueave/SeamAlgebra.lean)

In Uwueave/Confluence.lean, Ember models replica states as a join-semilattice (MergeState S) equipped with an operational reachability step Step : S → S → Prop and an invariant predicate I : S → Prop:

lean
class MergeState (S : Type u) where
  join : S → S → S
  join_comm : ∀ a b : S, join a b = join b a
  join_assoc : ∀ a b c : S, join (join a b) c = join a (join b c)
  join_idem : ∀ a : S, join a a = a

infixl:65 " ⊔ " => MergeState.join

def Valid {S : Type u} (Step : S → S → Prop) (I : S → Prop) (s : S) : Prop :=
  I s ∧ ∀ s', Step s s' → I s'

def Closed {S : Type u} [MergeState S] (I : S → Prop) (A : S → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : S, A x → A y → I x → I y → I (x ⊔ y)

def IConfluent {S : Type u} [MergeState S] (Step : S → S → Prop) (I : S → Prop) : Prop :=
  Closed I (Reachable Step I)

Ember first proves iconfluent_iff_pair_closed (showing $I$-confluence reduces to binary join closure on invariant-satisfying reachable states) and then exhibits a concrete counterexample to naive CRDT merge (escalation_witness, Uwueave/Confluence.lean): in a 2-slot permission Lattice EscalationState = Bool × Bool where the safety invariant AtMostOneAdmin (a, b) := !(a && b) forbids holding both slots simultaneously, replica 1 grants slot 1 ((true, false), valid) and replica 2 concurrently grants slot 2 ((false, true), valid), but their semilattice join (true, false) ⊔ (false, true) = (true, true) violates AtMostOneAdmin:

lean
theorem escalation_witness :
    ∃ x y : EscalationState,
      AtMostOneAdmin x ∧ AtMostOneAdmin y ∧ ¬ AtMostOneAdmin (x ⊔ y)

Segmented I-Confluence & Seam Algebra (Uwueave/SeamAlgebra.lean)

When an invariant $I$ is not globally $I$-confluent, how can replicas merge without coordinating on every operation? In Uwueave/SeamAlgebra.lean, Ember introduces a seam projection $\sigma : S \to K$ that maps each state $s \in S$ to a coordination fiber (or "color/epoch key") $\sigma(s) \in K$. Two states $x, y$ are allowed to merge coordination-free if and only if they lie in the same seam fiber ($\sigma(x) = \sigma(y)$); crossing a seam boundary ($\sigma(x) \ne \sigma(y)$) triggers explicit coordination (a barrier, arbiter cut, or prompt):

lean
def SegmentedIConfluent {S : Type u} {K : Type v} [MergeState S]
    (σ : S → K) (I : S → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : S, I x → I y → σ x = σ y → I (x ⊔ y)

def SeamStable {S : Type u} {K : Type v} [MergeState S]
    (σ : S → K) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : S, σ x = σ y → σ (x ⊔ y) = σ x

def SeamStableOn {S : Type u} {K : Type v} [MergeState S]
    (I : S → Prop) (σ : S → K) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : S, I x → I y → σ x = σ y → σ (x ⊔ y) = σ x

Uwueave/SeamAlgebra.lean proves a complete algebra of seams—along with negative counterexamples showing which laws fail without side conditions:

  1. Product Composition (product_segmented): If $\sigma_1 : S \to K_1$ segments $I_1$ and $\sigma_2 : S \to K_2$ segments $I_2$, then the product seam $\langle \sigma_1, \sigma_2 \rangle : S \to K_1 \times K_2$ segments $I_1 \wedge I_2$:
lean
   theorem product_segmented {S : Type u} {K₁ : Type v} {K₂ : Type w} [MergeState S]
       (σ₁ : S → K₁) (σ₂ : S → K₂) (I₁ I₂ : S → Prop)
       (h₁ : SegmentedIConfluent σ₁ I₁) (h₂ : SegmentedIConfluent σ₂ I₂) :
       SegmentedIConfluent (fun s => (σ₁ s, σ₂ s)) (fun s => I₁ s ∧ I₂ s)
  1. Why Coarsening/Refinement is Asymmetric (refinement_fails): Any finer seam $\sigma'$ that factors through $\sigma$ ($f \circ \sigma' = \sigma$) preserves SegmentedIConfluent, whereas coarsening a seam can merge clashing fibers and break confluence (theorem refinement_fails).
  2. Seam Substitution (seam_substitute) & Linked Seams (linked_segmented): If $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ induce the same kernel equivalence relation on $I$-valid states ($\forall x\,y,\; I x \to I y \to (\sigma_1 x = \sigma_1 y \leftrightarrow \sigma_2 x = \sigma_2 y)$), segmentation and SeamStableOn transfer across them (seam_substitute).
  3. Left-Projection Characterization (left_only_seam_iff): When composing two invariants $I_1 \wedge I_2$, eliding the second seam component ($\text{fst} \circ \langle \sigma_1, \sigma_2 \rangle = \sigma_1$) is valid if and only if $I_2$ is already closed on every $\sigma_1$-fiber (left_only_seam_iff).

2.3 The Clash-Graph Seam Solver (Uwueave/SeamColoring.lean)

In Uwueave/SeamColoring.lean (1,217 lines), Ember connects concurrent merge safety to graph coloring on the clash graph of invariant-violating joins.

The Clash Graph & The Fundamental Equivalence (segmented_iff_properColoring)

Given an invariant $I : S \to \text{Prop}$, two states $x, y \in S$ clash (Clashes I x y) if each individually satisfies $I$ but their semilattice join $x \⊔ y$ violates $I$:

lean
def Clashes {S : Type u} [MergeState S] (I : S → Prop) (x y : S) : Prop :=
  I x ∧ I y ∧ ¬ I (x ⊔ y)

theorem clashes_symm {S : Type u} [MergeState S] {I : S → Prop} {x y : S} :
    Clashes I x y → Clashes I y x

theorem clashes_irrefl {S : Type u} [MergeState S] {I : S → Prop} (x : S) :
    ¬ Clashes I x x

theorem iconfluent_iff_no_clash_edge {S : Type u} [MergeState S]
    (V : List S) (I : S → Prop) :
    (∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, I x → I y → I (x ⊔ y)) ↔
      (∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, ¬ Clashes I x y)

A seam $\sigma : S \to K$ is a proper coloring (ProperColoring V σ I) of the clash graph on carrier $V$ if no two clashing states receive the same seam color: $$\text{ProperColoring}(V, \sigma, I) \;:=\; \forall x \in V,\; \forall y \in V,\; \text{Clashes}(I, x, y) \implies \sigma(x) \ne \sigma(y)$$

Ember then proves the central duality theorem of leanuweave (Uwueave/SeamColoring.lean):

  • Without SeamStableOn, proper graph coloring of pairwise clashes does not suffice for multi-step segmented confluence, because joining two compatible states $x, y$ in color $c$ could produce a state $x \⊔ y$ whose color drifts to $c' \ne c$, colliding with a third state $z$ (coloring_alone_does_not_segment).
  • With SeamStableOn, segmented $I$-confluence is equivalent to proper clash-graph coloring (segmented_iff_properColoring):
lean
theorem coloring_alone_does_not_segment :
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : MergeState S) (V : List S) (I : S → Prop) (σ : S → Nat),
      ProperColoring V σ I ∧ ¬ SeamStableOn I σ ∧
      ∃ x ∈ V, ∃ y ∈ V, ∃ z ∈ V,
        I x ∧ I y ∧ I z ∧ σ x = σ y ∧ σ (x ⊔ y) = σ z ∧ ¬ I ((x ⊔ y) ⊔ z)

theorem segmented_iff_properColoring {S : Type u} {K : Type v} [MergeState S]
    (V : List S) (σ : S → K) (I : S → Prop)
    (hV : ∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, x ⊔ y ∈ V) :
    (SegmentedIConfluentOn V σ I ∧ SeamStableOnV V I σ) ↔
      (ProperColoring V σ I ∧ SeamStableOnV V I σ)

Verified Greedy & Exact Minimum-Width Seam Synthesizers

Uwueave/SeamColoring.lean goes on to build two verified seam synthesizers over any finite carrier V : List S with decidable invariant Ib : S → Bool:

  1. Verified Greedy Coloring (greedySeamFor & synthesizeSeam?): Assigns each vertex $x \in V$ the smallest natural number color $c \in \mathbb{N}$ not already assigned to an earlier vertex $y$ that clashes with $x$, and checks SeamStableOn:
lean
   theorem greedySeamFor_properColoring {S : Type u} [DecidableEq S] [MergeState S]
       (V : List S) (Ib : S → Bool) (hNodup : V.Nodup) :
       ProperColoring V (greedySeamFor V Ib) (fun s => Ib s = true)
  1. Exact Minimum-Chromatic-Width Synthesizer (synthesizeMinimumSeam): Because each distinct seam color corresponds to a coordination boundary (an epoch/barrier class), minimizing coordination overhead requires finding the chromatic number $\chi(G_{\text{clash}})$ among all SeamStableOn-respecting colorings. synthesizeMinimumSeam enumerates bounded colorings by increasing width $k = 1, 2, \dots, |V|$ and proves both totality (minimumSeam_search_total) and exact optimality (pin_minimum_is_exact—no valid stable coloring exists with fewer colors than the synthesized minimum).

2.4 Multi-Currency Schedule Synthesis & Bounded Synthesis Obligations

The 5-Currency Cost Lattice (Uwueave/ScheduleSynthesis.lean)

When a concurrent execution crosses a seam boundary, different coordination mechanisms incur costs in different operational currencies. In Uwueave/ScheduleSynthesis.lean, Ember defines a 5-currency vector budget over:

lean
inductive Currency where
  | peerBarrier   -- symmetric peer-to-peer synchronization barrier
  | arbiterCut    -- serialized cut through a designated arbiter replica
  | networkRound  -- additional wide-area message round-trip
  | userPrompt    -- interactive conflict-resolution prompt surfaced to user
  | rollback      -- speculative execution abort and replay
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

A candidate schedule profile p : Profile is checked against a multi-currency budget b : Budget via componentwise dominance Fits b p ($\forall c,\; p(c) \le b(c)$), with explicit counterexample witness Violates b p. The synthesizer selectLeast searches a finite candidate catalog and returns a strongly typed sum:

  • SearchResult.found p: accompanied by a proof Fits b p and a Pareto/lexicographic minimality certificate LeastResult proving no feasible candidate in the catalog strictly dominates p.
  • SearchResult.exhausted: accompanied by a universal refutation certificate proving $\forall p \in \text{catalog},\; \text{Violates}\; b\; p$.

Finite-Product Search & Quota Admission (FiniteProductSearch.lean, FiniteProductClosure.lean)

To prevent state-space explosion when composing multiple concurrent subsystems, Uwueave/FiniteProductSearch.lean and Uwueave/FiniteProductClosure.lean formalize:

  • Carrier.Limits & Capped: hard cardinality caps on product carriers (maxStates, maxEdges, maxColors).
  • MaximumClique & MaximumLiveClique: exact clique lower-bound certificates on the clash graph (proving by weak duality that $\chi(G_{\text{clash}}) \ge \omega(G_{\text{clash}})$, so any budget permitting fewer than $|\text{clique}|$ seam fibers is immediately refutable without coloring search).
  • QuotaCheck, CatalogAdmission, and ClosedScope: certified admission gates that reject any protocol composition whose reachable state product or seam width exceeds its declared envelope.

3.2 The 474-Line Micro-Kernel Metamath Verifier (src/kernel.rs)

To guarantee that no tactic, polynomial normalizer, or DAG cruncher can ever introduce an unsound step, src/kernel.rs implements a standalone, zero-dependency Metamath RPN proof verifier from scratch in 474 lines of Rust:

rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Kind { F, E, A, P }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Stmt {
    pub label: String,
    pub kind: Kind,
    pub expr: Vec<String>,          // tokens starting with typecode ("wff", "term", "|-")
    pub mand_hyps: Vec<String>,     // mandatory $f and $e labels in declaration order
    pub dv: Vec<(String, String)>,  // mandatory disjoint-variable pairs ($d)
    pub proof: Vec<String>,         // uncompressed RPN label sequence (for Kind::P)
}

pub struct Db {
    pub consts: HashSet<String>,
    pub vars: HashSet<String>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
    pub by_label: HashMap<String, usize>,
}

When Db::verify(&self) (src/kernel.rs) checks a $p statement st, verify_one executes the standard Metamath stack machine:

  1. Each label step in st.proof is looked up in by_label (checking that step precedes st in the database so forward/circular references are impossible).
  2. If step is an active $f or $e hypothesis, its token vector expr is pushed onto the RPN stack.
  3. If step is an $a or $p assertion with $m = \text{mand\_hyps.len()}$ mandatory hypotheses, verify_one pops $m$ entries from stack:
  4. For each mandatory $f hypothesis [tc, var], it checks that the popped stack entry has matching typecode tc and binds subst.insert(var, popped[1..]).
  5. For each mandatory $d pair (v1, v2) on step, it collects all variables occurring in subst[v1] and subst[v2], checks they are syntactically distinct (x != y), and verifies that (x, y) is declared in the current theorem's $d frame.
  6. For each mandatory $e hypothesis, it applies subst to the $e expression and checks token-for-token equality against the popped stack entry.
  7. Finally, it applies subst to step.expr and pushes the resulting conclusion onto stack.
  8. At the end of st.proof, verify_one checks stack.len() == 1 && stack[0] == st.expr.

3.3 Proof-Term Elaboration, Peephole Shrinking & Deduction-Form Combinators (src/elaborate.rs, src/bin/grounded.rs)

Writing 7.25 million Metamath RPN steps by hand is impossible; writing an unverified custom decision procedure forfeits formal trust. Ember bridged this gap in src/elaborate.rs and src/bin/grounded.rs with an untrusted-convenience, kernel-rechecked elaborator (Elab) over recursive proof trees Pt { label: String, kids: Vec<Pt> }.

Named-Binding Application & Deduction-Form Combinators (src/elaborate.rs)

Instead of manually ordering positional $f and $e stack arguments, Elab::app (src/elaborate.rs) accepts named variable bindings binds: &[(&str, Pt)] and essential subproofs ess: &[Pt], validates that every key in binds is an actual mandatory $f variable of label, orders children in exact kernel declaration order, and computes conclusions via Elab::conclusion_l.

In commits b106088 and 17e5229 (2026-05-15/16, src/elaborate.rs), Ember distilled seven recurring Hilbert-system proof patterns discovered across the G1/G2/G3 derivations into self-typing combinators that recover their wff/term syntax trees directly by parsing premise conclusions:

Sound Peephole Proof-Tree Shrinker (shrink_pt, src/elaborate.rs)

Before flattening a Pt to RPN, shrink_pt (src/elaborate.rs) applies four bottom-up, conclusion-preserving algebraic peephole rules to a fixpoint:

  • Rule 1 (eqtr(x, x, z; eqid(x), p2) ↦ p2): Transitivity whose left premise is reflexivity x = x collapses to the right premise p2 : x = z.
  • Rule 2 (eqtr(x, y, y; p1, eqid(y)) ↦ p1): Symmetric right-eqid collapse.
  • Rule 3 (eqtr(x, x, x; eqid(x), eqid(x)) ↦ eqid(x)): Double reflexivity collapse.
  • Rule 4 (Double eqcom round-trip): ax-mp detaching eqcom(b, a) against ax-mp detaching eqcom(a, b) on q : a = b collapses directly to q.

The Kernel-Checked ring_eq Polynomial Normalizer (src/bin/grounded.rs)

Every coordinate-geometry identity in grounded.rs, proof_g1.rs, proof_g2.rs, and proof_g3.rs is proved by ring_eq(el, &lhs, &rhs) (src/bin/grounded.rs), which emits a step-by-step Hilbert proof of |- lhs = rhs using only the ordered-ring axioms (of-addcom, of-addass, of-add0, of-addinv, of-mulcom, of-mulass, of-distr, df-sub) and congruence/transitivity lemmas:

  1. Subtraction Desugaring: Rewrites u -x v into u + (0 -x v) via df-sub.
  2. Distribution & Sign Canonicalization: Pushes products across sums (of-distr) and pulls negation (0 -x u) outside monomials via mulneg1, mulneg2, negadd, and negneg.
  3. Multiplicative AC Normalization: Flattens each *-monomial into its multiset of atomic factors, right-associates (of-mulass), and bubble-sorts factors into canonical token order (of-mulcom).
  4. Additive AC Normalization & Cancellation: Flattens the +-tree (flatten), sorts signed monomials (ra_sort, optimized in commit 461b7c9 to $O(n)$ endpoint-threading swap_terms so cargo run --release --bin grounded finishes in 2.02 seconds), cancels opposite pairs m + (0 -x m) = 0 (of-addinv), and eliminates zeros (of-add0).

The Generic Template Pattern (gen_inst) Against Degree Blowup: Expanding a degree-8 polynomial over 2D point differences (Xc b -x Xc a) directly inside ring_eq would generate millions of intermediate monomial swaps. Ember documented an explicit numerical counterexample (b-a = (-1.3, 0.7), c-a = (2.0, 0.5), x-a = (0.9, -2.561073825503356) where ACong holds with EQ = 0 and positive dot-sign 6.67 >= 0, yet the collinearity determinant is -5.57 != 0), and then proved the exact oriented postulate G3bp-protuniq-oriented (628,987 steps) by adjoining the half-plane orientation sign 0 <_ (crs b a c b a x) via the conservative cross-product definition df-crs.

3.5 The Sound Proof-DAG CSE Minimizer (src/cse.rs) & set.mm ZFC Model Splice (src/bin/modelsplice.rs)

Sound Proof-DAG Crunching (src/cse.rs, commit e693b40)

In src/cse.rs, Ember implemented cse::crunch(src: &str) -> String, a post-elaboration common-subexpression eliminator that factors repeated closed RPN subtrees across all 87 $p proofs into shared helper lemmas cse0, cse1, ...:

  • Parses each $p statement's RPN token stream into an explicit arity tree (build_tree) and computes a bottom-up 128-bit FNV-1a structural hash (u64, u64) for every subtree.
  • Closed-Subproof Guard (ok[i]): Ensures a candidate subtree contains zero local $e hypothesis leaves (since a shared helper $p outside ${ $} cannot depend on another theorem's scoped $e assumptions) and derives a |- judgement (not a bare wff or term syntax tree).
  • Ranks repeated subtrees by net token savings (occurrences - 1) * (subtree_len - 1) - (subtree_len + header_cost), emits positive-savings helpers before their first user, and performs a single linear-time top-down rewrite pass.
  • Authoritative Kernel Gate (src/bin/grounded.rs): emit_json re-parses the crunched .mm corpus into a fresh kernel::Db, runs cdb.verify(), and checks that all 87 original $p theorems have byte-identical statement conclusions before accepting the crunched DAG size (9,229,237 $\to$ 9,137,749 shared steps, saving 91,488 RPN steps).

The set.mm ZFC Model Splice & resqrtth Attribution (src/bin/modelsplice.rs)

In src/bin/modelsplice.rs, Ember parses the full Metamath set.mm database (~40,000+ theorems) and binds all 12 non-conservative F1 axioms (of-addcom $\mapsto$ addcom, of-addass $\mapsto$ addass, ..., of-sqpos $\mapsto$ msqge0, ax-sqrt $\mapsto$ resqrtth) to their ZFC proofs over constructed $\mathbb{R}$.

Using exact arbitrary-precision bignum arithmetic (ProofSize in src/number.rs), modelsplice.rs reveals three foundational results:

  1. Completeness (ax-sup / ax-pre-sup) is NOT required: Even resqrtth ($\sqrt{a} \cdot \sqrt{a} = a$ for $0 \le a$) is proved in set.mm without invoking extra axioms beyond ZFC; its $10^{45.7}$ cut-free size comes from analytic construction multiplicity (many invocations of the same ZFC primitives through Dedekind cuts and limits), not from a stronger axiom system.
  2. Occurrence-Level Bipartition of resqrtth (Task #9, src/bin/modelsplice.rs): By partitioning every path in the expanded ZFC DAG of resqrtth into (a) paths passing through Dedekind/Cauchy/LUB completion anchors (df-np, df-nr, df-sup, df-clim, etc.) versus (b) completion-free $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ pair-plumbing and FOL/set glue, Ember proved that (a) + (b) == total holds with exact bignum equality and that the $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ pair-plumbing + FOL equality multiplicity accounts for the overwhelming bulk of any constructed field in ZFC.
  3. Wholesale Euclidean Primitive Reduction: Replacing resqrtth with a minimal Euclidean field model (where $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is a model primitive via algebraic field extensions) drops the substrate cost by nearly 9 orders of magnitude from $\sim 10^{45.7}$ to $\sim 10^{37.0}$ (dominated by msqge0, $0 \le a \cdot a$).

Part IV: Adjacent Formal & Categorical Strands (navier-stokes-proof, ergolang, bead-calculus)

4.1 navier-stokes-proof & worktrees/ns-energy-cancellation — Torus PDE Calculus & Nonlinear Energy Cancellation in Lean 4

In /Users/ember/dev/navier-stokes-proof (README.md, FORMALIZATION.md, DYNAMICS.md) and /Users/ember/dev/worktrees/ns-energy-cancellation (commit 7190276, 2026-08-17), Ember (ember arlynx) conducted the first external mathematical and formal review (PR #1) of Jeffrey S. Cambria's paper Global Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Incompressible Navier–Stokes Equations on the Torus, and went on to build a 978-theorem Lean 4 PDE formalization (1,067 kernel-checked theorems total in lean/NSFormal over pinned Mathlib v4.33.0, zero sorrys).

1. The Viscous-Term Erratum & Maximum-Envelope Repair (NSFormal/VorticityMaximum.lean, MaxEnvelope.lean)

In PR #1 (README.md), Ember identified a critical analytic error in §3.1, §10, and §16.2 of v001 of the paper: the paper had written the pointwise vorticity-magnitude evolution as the inviscid identity $D_t|\omega| = \alpha|\omega|$, omitting the viscous term $\nu \xi \cdot \Delta\omega$: $$D_t|\omega| = \alpha|\omega| + \nu \xi \cdot \Delta\omega, \qquad \xi = \frac{\omega}{|\omega|}$$ Because $\nu \xi \cdot \Delta\omega$ is not globally nonpositive along an arbitrary particle trajectory, the per-trajectory Grönwall chain in v001 failed as written. However, at spatial maximizers of $|\omega(t, \cdot)|^2 / 2$ on the compact three-torus $\mathbb{T}^3$, transport $(u \cdot \nabla)(|\omega|^2/2)$ vanishes by Fermat's theorem and the scalar Laplacian $\Delta(|\omega|^2/2)$ is nonpositive by the second-derivative test, while $\langle \omega, \Delta\omega \rangle = \Delta(|\omega|^2/2) - |\nabla\omega|^2 \le 0$.

Ember formalized this complete repair in Lean 4 across:

  • NSFormal/Domain.lean: Defines Torus3 := Fin 3 → AddCircle (2 * Real.pi) and proves compactness and nonemptiness.
  • NSFormal/MaxEnvelope.lean: Proves a compact-domain Danskin theorem bounding upper right Dini derivatives of the spatial maximum envelope $M(t) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{T}^3} f(t, x)$ by the supremum of $\partial_t f(t, x)$ over the current compact maximizer set, followed by an integrating-factor Grönwall closure that never assumes a differentiable maximizer trajectory $x_{\max}(t)$.
  • NSFormal/PeriodicCalculus.lean & NSFormal/VorticityMaximum.lean: Uses the smooth energy density $|\omega|^2/2$ to avoid the singular direction $\omega/|\omega|$ at zeros and proves the exact parabolic identity $\langle \omega, \Delta\omega \rangle = \Delta(|\omega|^2/2) - |\nabla\omega|^2$.

2. Concrete Haar Periodic Integration by Parts (NSFormal/PeriodicIntegration.lean & ForTauCeti/PeriodicIntegration.lean)

Rather than axiomatizing skew-adjointness of $\partial_i$ on $\mathbb{T}^3$, NSFormal/PeriodicIntegration.lean and the generalized extraction module NSFormal/ForTauCeti/PeriodicIntegration.lean (commit 625c717) prove integration by parts from Mathlib's AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval on $[0, T]$, transport it via AddCircle.integral_liftIoc_eq_intervalIntegral to Haar measure on AddCircle T, and lift it via Mathlib's measure-preserving coordinate split MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (unitTorus_volume_preserving_coordinate_split) and Fubini's theorem to both Torus3 and arbitrary-dimension UnitAddTorus (Fin (n + 1)):

lean
theorem addCircle_integral_mul_deriv_eq_neg_deriv_mul_of_periodic
    {T : ℝ} [Fact (0 < T)] {f g : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (hg : ContDiff ℝ 1 g)
    (hfper : Periodic f T) (hgper : Periodic g T) :
    (∫ x : AddCircle T,
        AddCircle.liftIoc T 0 (fun r => f r * deriv g r) x) =
      -(∫ x : AddCircle T,
        AddCircle.liftIoc T 0 (fun r => deriv f r * g r) x)

theorem unitTorus_integral_mul_coordinateDerivative_eq_neg
    (f g : UnitAddTorus (Fin (n + 1)) → ℝ) (i : Fin (n + 1))
    (hf : ∀ y : UnitTorusCoordinateComplement n,
      ContDiff ℝ 1 (unitTorusCoordinateSliceLift f i y))
    (hg : ∀ y : UnitTorusCoordinateComplement n,
      ContDiff ℝ 1 (unitTorusCoordinateSliceLift g i y))
    (hfg : Integrable (fun x => f x * unitTorusCoordinateDerivative g i x))
    (hgf : Integrable (fun x => unitTorusCoordinateDerivative f i x * g x)) :
    (∫ x, f x * unitTorusCoordinateDerivative g i x) =
      -(∫ x, unitTorusCoordinateDerivative f i x * g x)

3. Global Enstrophy Balance & Dynamic Quotient Continuation (Enstrophy.lean, DynamicCriterion.lean)

In NSFormal/Enstrophy.lean, Ember proves that the slice derivative used by Haar integration equals the lifted Fréchet partial derivative torusPartial even across the quotient seam (torusCoordinateDerivative_eq_torusPartial), constructs Haar integration as a continuous linear map on $C(\mathbb{T}^3, \mathbb{R})$ so time differentiation under the integral sign follows directly from the chain rule, and derives the global enstrophy balance: $$E'(t) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \omega \cdot (\omega \cdot \nabla) u \, dx - \nu \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} |\nabla\omega|^2 \, dx$$ In NSFormal/DynamicCriterion.lean, Ember proves the logarithmic Grönwall continuation criterion quotient_cubic_rate_bounded_of_energy_budget ($E' \le C \Theta^2 E^3$ and $\Theta^2 E \le M$ with $\int_a^t E \le B \implies E(t) \le E(a)\exp(CMB)$ via $(\log E)' \le CME$) alongside the exact Hilbert-space Cauchy defect identity integral_cauchy_defect_eq_scaled_projection_residual.

4.2 ergolang — Programs as Sheaf Sections (ergo.pl, prelude.ergo)

In /Users/ember/dev/ergolang (README.md, ergo.pl, prelude.ergo), Ember designed and implemented Ergolang: a symbolic language in SWI-Prolog where programs are collections of local sections over a context space, and composition failure is measured as quantitative defect ($\Delta$) rather than thrown as a fatal exception.

Context State, Material Parameters & Semantic Charges (ergo.pl)

Every evaluation region in ergo.pl is a state tuple ctx(Id, Parent, Sections, Waves, Eta, Kappa, Delta, Mode):

  • Sections: AVL association map (library(assoc)) of committed local facts Name -> Value.
  • Waves: AVL association map of uncollapsed superpositions Name -> wave(Branches) or deferred(Expr).
  • Viscosity $\eta \in [0, 1]$ (Eta): Controls defect containment across section boundaries. When a child section or block finishes with defect $\Delta_{\text{child}}$, the defect propagated to the enclosing parent context is damped by $1 - \eta$ (ergo.pl, L505-L515): $$\Delta_{\text{parent}}' = \Delta_{\text{parent}} + (1 - \eta)\,\Delta_{\text{child}}$$ At $\eta = 1.0$ (section incoherent(eta=1.0, kappa=0.0) in prelude.ergo), contradictions remain completely local; at $\eta = 0.0$ (section coherence(eta=0.0, kappa=1.0)), all defect escapes to the parent.
  • Permeability $\kappa \in [0, 1]$ (Kappa): Controls cross-boundary dereferencing (@ref requires $\kappa > 0.5$ for deep ancestor lookup, else incurs a $+0.1$ defect penalty on local miss, ergo.pl), parent fact propagation on <! assert-bindings ($\kappa > 0.7$, L580-L589), and wave collapse thermodynamics.

Sheaf Gluing (=>>) & Coalgebraic Observation Backreaction (?)

  1. Gluing & Overlap Defect (coherence_check & glue_values, ergo.pl): When two sections or values $V_1, V_2$ are glued via E1 =>> E2 or !assert, overlaps/2 checks if they bind the same functor/atom name. If they agree on overlaps (compatible(V1, V2)), they glue cleanly with $\Delta = 0.0$. If they disagree (e.g., physics_si asserting !c(299792458) vs. physics_natural asserting !c(1)), measure_incompatibility computes the normalized structural distance: $$\Delta(V_1, V_2) = \min\!\left(1.0,\; \frac{\text{structure\_distance}(V_1, V_2)}{10.0}\right)$$ and accumulates $\Delta$ into the context without halting execution.
  2. Observation with Backreaction (observe/4, ergo.pl): Querying a superposition wave(Branches) with $N = |\text{Branches}|$ via ?expr is a coalgebraic transition $\alpha : \text{State} \to \text{Obs} \times \text{State}$ that collapses the wave according to $\kappa$ (uniform random for $\kappa > 0.7$, lowest-energy first branch for $\kappa < 0.3$, biased mixture for $0.3 \le \kappa \le 0.7$) and increments $\Delta$ by the thermodynamic observation cost: $$\Delta_{\text{obs}} = 0.1 \cdot (1 - \kappa) \cdot \log_2(N)$$

4.3 bead-calculus — Traced Monoidal String Diagrams as Kinetic Marble Machines

In /Users/ember/dev/bead-calculus (README, LEVEL_UP.md, src/core/diagram.ts, src/core/rewrite.ts, src/core/invariant.ts), Ember built an interactive string-diagram rewrite and simulation engine where morphisms in a traced symmetric monoidal / compact-closed category are realized as kinetic marble machines.

Categorical Dictionary & Diagram Representation (src/core/diagram.ts)

In src/core/diagram.ts, a Diagram consists of typed Port channels (BeadKind: 'red' | 'blue' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'purple' | 'orange' | 'cyan' | 'white' | 'black' | 'signal'), 21 gate NodeType primitives (identity, swap, delay, split, merge, trace-in, trace-out, unit, counit, cup, cap, painter, filter, mixer, clock, sync, splitter, queue, valve, bleacher, membrane), directed Edge wires, feedback TracePair loops ($\text{Tr}_{A,B}^X(f)$), and compact-closed CupCapPair duals ($\eta_X : I \to X^* \otimes X$, $\varepsilon_X : X \otimes X^* \to I$).

The 6 Sound Local Graph-Rewrite Rules (src/core/rewrite.ts)

In src/core/rewrite.ts (commits c5e47c8 and ca9ca38), Ember implemented six local pattern-matching and graph-transformation rules corresponding to the coherence laws of traced symmetric monoidal and compact-closed categories:

straightenYanking (Vanishing II): $\operatorname{Tr}^X(\mathrm{id}_X) = \mathrm{id}_X$findStraightenMatches / applyStraighten (L82-L219)isEmptyTrace(diagram, tracePair) verifies trace-in.outputs[0] connects directly and uniquely to trace-out.inputs[0], splicing incoming and outgoing wires directly.

§0. Scope, Methodology & Primary Repository Ledger

Across five interlocking repositories created between January and September 2026, Ember developed a unified computational biology and biophysics research program: compiling real biological wiring diagrams, physiological control loops, and sensory coding constraints into deterministic, hardware-accelerated, proof-carrying simulations.

Where conventional "artificial life" or "bio-inspired AI" projects substitute toy multilayer perceptrons and reward heuristics for anatomy, Ember's biological strand enforces strict mechanistic fidelity (NO QUICK FIXES / ALWAYS PURSUE MECHANISTIC VALIDITY / ALWAYS GROUND IN LITERATURE REFERENCES- THE NEWER THE BETTER / USE DETAILED COMPUTATIONAL MODELS, /Users/ember/dev/humanbody/CLAUDE.md:1-7):

  1. Invertebrate Connectomics & Embodied Biophysics (/Users/ember/dev/chreatures): Compiles the complete adult Drosophila melanogaster central nervous system (MaleCNS v1.0: 165,122 traced neurons, 25,563,197 directed synaptic edges, 124,025,046 synapses) and pairs it with the adult micro-CT NeuroMechFly v2.1.0 body (69 anatomical segments, 126 hinge DOFs, 90 physical MuJoCo actuators, 807 nonvisual sensory channels, and 1,771 bilateral retinal hex columns anchored to 3,936 R1–R8 photoreceptors) plus a 4,184-edge plastic mushroom-body $\gamma 1\text{pedc}$ circuit (KC -> MBON11 gated by dopaminergic PPL101) running across 12 native Rust/Metal/WebGPU/Wasm crates.
  2. Mammalian Cardiorespiratory & Autonomic Control (/Users/ember/dev/brorb & /Users/ember/dev/humanbody): Couples a 5-population, 10-ODE medullary respiratory Central Pattern Generator (Molkov et al. 2017 / Rubin et al. 2011) with 3-state lung mechanics, Hering-Breuer stretch reflexes, Severinghaus-Hill oxyhemoglobin dissociation, medullary RTN + carotid body chemoreception, Nucleus Ambiguus cardiac vagal motor neurons generating emergent Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (RSA), Frank-Starling stroke volume, Windkessel hemodynamics, coronary perfusion/ischemia cascades, and AudioWorklet microphone breath entrainment.

The Kenyon Cell Sign Bug & known_nt Precedence: In scripts/build_connectome.py:130-166, Ember identified a critical biological pitfall in raw machine-predicted neurotransmitter tables: FlyWire's top_nt column misclassifies 5,168 of 5,177 Kenyon cells as dopamine (which would assign them sign 0 in fast synaptic recurrence and silence the mushroom body), whereas curated experimental ground truth (known_nt, Barnstedt et al. 2016) establishes that Kenyon cells are cholinergic (acetylcholine, excitatory +1). build_connectome.py therefore resolves known_nt first and falls back to top_nt only when known_nt is empty:

  • Excitatory (+1): acetylcholine
  • Inhibitory (-1): gaba, glutamate (inhibitory GluCl channels in the insect CNS)
  • Modulatory (0 in fast matrix W_exc/W_inh, routed to modulatory traces): dopamine, serotonin, octopamine

2.3 CNS Dynamics V2: Operating-Point-Relative Recurrence & Rank-64 Readout

In CNS Dynamics V2 (docs/development/CNS_DYNAMICS_V2.md:1-155, research/dynamics_v2/README.md), Ember replaced uniform global leak constants with a cell-type-specific operating-point formulation over 11,752 distinct cell types (graph.type_id[N]). Each cell type $c \in \{0, \dots, 11751\}$ stores 5 raw unconstrained parameters mapped via $\sigma(z) = (1 + e^{-z})^{-1}$ into biophysically bounded intervals:

$$r_0(c) = 0.05 + 0.40\,\sigma(\theta_{r_0, c}), \quad g(c) = 0.50 + 1.50\,\sigma(\theta_{g, c}), \quad \tau(c) = 0.02 + 0.23\,\sigma(\theta_{\tau, c})$$
$$k(c) = 0.50\,\sigma(\theta_{k, c}), \quad \tau_a(c) = 0.25 + 4.75\,\sigma(\theta_{\tau_a, c})$$

Crucially, presynaptic efficacy is driven by deviation from the cell type's baseline operating point $x_i = r_i - r_{0, i}$ rather than raw rate $r_i$. Over two Jacobi substeps per tick ($\Delta t_{\text{sub}} = \Delta t / 2$), with neutral_drive[j] precomputed so that $r = r_0, a = 0$ is an exact fixed point under neutral sensory input:

$$\text{rec}_j = \sum_{e \in \text{row}(j)} W_e \cdot (r_{\text{src}(e)} - r_{0, \text{src}(e)}), \qquad u_j = (\text{afferent}_j - \text{neutral\_drive}_j) + g_j \cdot \text{rec}_j - k_j \cdot a_j$$
$$s_j = \begin{cases} 1 - r_{0, j} & \text{if } u_j \ge 0 \\ r_{0, j} & \text{if } u_j < 0 \end{cases}, \qquad h_j = \max(s_j, 0.05), \qquad r_j^{\text{target}} = \text{clamp}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(r_{0, j} + s_j \, h_j \tanh\!\left(\frac{u_j}{h_j}\right)\right)$$
$$r_j \leftarrow r_j + \frac{\Delta t_{\text{sub}}}{\tau_j}\left(r_j^{\text{target}} - r_j\right), \qquad a_j \leftarrow a_j + \frac{\Delta t_{\text{sub}}}{\tau_{a, j}}\left(|r_j - r_{0, j}| - a_j\right)$$

To project all 165,122 neurons into the 512-channel latent vector Z512 without an intractable $512 \times 165,122$ dense matrix, V2 introduces a rank-64 factorized readout (V of shape [64, 165122], U of shape [512, 64], row emphasis m[165122], and bias b[512]):

$$z_{\text{lat}} = V \cdot \left(m \odot (r - r_0)\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{64}, \qquad Z_{512} = \tanh(U \cdot z_{\text{lat}} + b) \in (-1, 1)^{512}$$

2.4 Anatomical CNS V3: Synaptic Release Availability $q$ & Tri-Monoaminergic Traces

Anatomical CNS V3 (docs/development/ANATOMICAL_CNS_V3.md:1-180, research/anatomical_cns/README.md:1-140) expanded the per-resident state to 7 fields (r, a, q, mDA, mOA, mHT, z) and the cell-type parameter table from 5 to 13 columns ([11752, 13]):

  • Presynaptic Release Availability $q_i \in [0.05, 1.0]$: Models short-term synaptic depression (vesicle depletion) with recovery time constant $\tau_{r, i} = 0.05 + 1.95\,\sigma(\theta_{\text{tr}, i})$ and release fraction $u_{\text{se}, i} = 0.01 + 0.49\,\sigma(\theta_{\text{use}, i})$: $$\text{effective\_source}_i = (r_i - r_{0, i}) \cdot q_i, \qquad \frac{dq_i}{dt} = \frac{1 - q_i}{\tau_{r, i}} - u_{\text{se}, i} \cdot q_i \cdot \max(r_i - r_{0, i}, 0)$$
  • Channel-Split CSR Accumulation (graph.channel[N] u32): Each neuron is tagged with a neurotransmitter channel (0 = unknown, 1 = fast ACh/GABA/Glu, 2 = DA dopamine, 3 = OA octopamine, 4 = 5HT serotonin). During the CSR row traversal for target neuron $j$, edges from channel == 1 accumulate into fast_rec_j, while edges from channels 2, 3, 4 accumulate rectified positive source activity $\max(r_i - r_{0, i}, 0) \cdot q_i \cdot |W_e|$ into target-local monoamine drives drive_DA, drive_OA, drive_HT.
  • Target Modulatory Traces (mDA, mOA, mHT): Relax with time constants $\tau_{\text{DA}} = 0.20 + 1.80\,\sigma$, $\tau_{\text{OA}} = 0.20 + 2.80\,\sigma$, $\tau_{\text{HT}} = 0.30 + 3.70\,\sigma$ toward $\tanh(\text{drive})$ and dynamically rescale each neuron's recurrent gain and adaptation: $$g_{\text{eff}, j} = g_j \cdot \text{clamp}_{[0.25, 2.5]}\!\left(1 + \gamma_{\text{DA}, j} m_{\text{DA}, j} + \gamma_{\text{OA}, j} m_{\text{OA}, j} + \gamma_{\text{HT}, j} m_{\text{HT}, j}\right)$$ $$k_{\text{eff}, j} = k_j \cdot \text{clamp}_{[0.25, 2.5]}\!\left(1 - 0.5\,\alpha_{\text{OA}, j} m_{\text{OA}, j} + 0.5\,\alpha_{\text{HT}, j} m_{\text{HT}, j}\right)$$
  • Descending Context Interface (Context12): Rather than injecting task context globally, V3 restricts context modulation (12 scalars) exclusively to the 1,314 descending neurons via a centered zero-preserving transform: $$\text{context\_drive}_d = 0.15 \cdot \left(\tanh(W_{\text{ctx}, d} \cdot c + b_{\text{ctx}, d}) - \tanh(b_{\text{ctx}, d})\right)$$ guaranteeing that when $c = \mathbf{0}$, $\text{context\_drive}_d \equiv 0$.

In Embodied CNS V4 (docs/development/FLY_BODY_ANATOMY.md:1-145, native/fly-body/README.md), Ember performed a rigorous anatomical join between the adult male MaleCNS v1.0 connectome and the adult female micro-CT FlyGym / NeuroMechFly v2.1.0 biomechanical model (upstream commit ca65a510c2afe6ac61c51df4f274c8d190c2f95f, 1:1 physical scale where 1 MJCF length unit = 1 mm, mass in kg, time in s, YAW-PITCH-ROLL joint ordering):

2.6 Lifetime-Learning CNS V5: Private Synaptic Plasticity in Mushroom Body $\gamma 1\text{pedc}$

To endow embodied flies with genuine lifetime associative learning without mutating the shared 25.56M-edge CSR connectome buffer, CNS V5 (docs/development/CNS_LIFETIME_LEARNING_WAVE.md:1-140, docs/MUSHROOM_PLASTICITY.md:1-120, data/mushroom/gamma1pedc-v5-plasticity-selector-v1.json) extracts the exact bilateral mushroom-body $\gamma 1\text{pedc}$ aversive/associative compartment directly from MaleCNS v1.0:

Postsynaptic Output (MBON11, $\gamma 1\text{pedc}>\alpha/\beta$)bodyId = 10704 (row = 655)bodyId = 11402 (row = 1306)2 MBON11 target rows
Presynaptic Kenyon Cells (KC -> MBON11)2,048 directed edges (16,863 synapses)2,136 directed edges (24,597 synapses)4,184 plastic edges (41,460 synapses from 3,623 connected KCs of 4,064 curated KCs)

The V5 Plasticity Math & Serial Determinism: Each resident maintains only 32.7 KiB of private plastic state (plastic_d[4184] f32 efficacy deviation in [-max_depression, 0] and plastic_e[4184] f32 eligibility trace in [0, 1]).

  1. Recurrent Correction at Both Jacobi Substeps: During each 5 ms halfstep, after the immutable CSR gather computes baseline fast_rec for row 655 (MBON11_L) and row 1306 (MBON11_R), V5 adds the plastic correction in canonical selector order (0..2048 for L, 2048..4184 for R): $$\Delta\text{rec}_{\text{MBON11}} = \sum_{p \in \text{selector}} W_{\text{base}}(p) \cdot d_p \cdot \left(r_{\text{KC}(p)} - r_{0, \text{KC}(p)}\right) \cdot q_{\text{KC}(p)}$$ Because MBON11 is GABAergic (channel = 1, inhibitory sign), depressing KC -> MBON11 ($d_p < 0$) disinhibits downstream premotor and valence circuits.
  2. Cue-Before-Gate Discrete Eligibility Update (rule = [0.8, 0.25, 0.8]): After the two Jacobi substeps complete for tick $\Delta t$, V5 updates $d_p$ and $e_p$ using the previous eligibility e_prev so that a simultaneous odor/visual cue and PPL101 gate cannot self-potentiate on the same tick (cue-before-gate causality, site/live/cns-webgpu.js:353-402, native/metal-brain/src/brain.metal:445-507): $$\text{cue}_p = \text{clamp}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(\frac{\max(r_{\text{KC}(p)} - r_{0, \text{KC}(p)}, 0)}{1 - r_{0, \text{KC}(p)}} \cdot q_{\text{KC}(p)}\right), \qquad \text{gate}_h = \text{clamp}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(\frac{\max(r_{\text{PPL101}, h} - r_{0, \text{PPL101}, h}, 0)}{1 - r_{0, \text{PPL101}, h}} \cdot q_{\text{PPL101}, h}\right)$$ $$d_p \leftarrow \text{clamp}_{[-d_{\max}, 0]}\!\left(d_p - \eta_{\text{dep}} \cdot \Delta t \cdot e_{\text{prev}, p} \cdot \text{gate}_{h(p)}\right), \qquad e_p \leftarrow \text{clamp}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(e_{\text{prev}, p} \cdot \exp\!\left(-\frac{\Delta t}{\tau_e}\right) + \text{cue}_p \cdot \left(1 - e_{\text{prev}, p} \cdot \exp\!\left(-\frac{\Delta t}{\tau_e}\right)\right)\right)$$ where $\tau_e = 0.8\text{ s}$, $\eta_{\text{dep}} = 0.25\text{ s}^{-1}$, and $d_{\max} = 0.8$.

§3. Embodied Sensory-Motor Physics: Bilateral Retinal Optics, Antennal Touch, Wing Acoustics & Aerodynamics

3.1 The Optic Input Anatomy Audit & OpticRetina (1,771 Bilateral Hex Columns)

In docs/development/OPTIC_INPUT_ANATOMY_AUDIT.md:1-130 (commits dc08a19 and de415bb), Ember audited the legacy retinal-v2 visual interface and uncovered two severe anatomical defects:

  1. retinal-v2 pooled 5$\times$16 peripheral rays into 320 ports that injected zero current into all 4,107 R1–R8 photoreceptors (R1-R6 = 2,953, R7 = 576, R8 = 578), bypassing the retina to stimulate L1/L2/L3/Mi/Tm lamina/medulla interneurons directly.
  2. build_retinal_encoder_v2.py lacked a hemisphere filter, causing a single spatial bin to stimulate both left and right optic lobes simultaneously.

To fix this from primary connectome metadata, Ember extracted the hexagonal ommatidial column assignments (assignedOlHex1, assignedOlHex2) across 23,720 optic-lobe intrinsic cells in MaleCNS v1.0:

  • This defines 1,771 bilateral retinal hex sites (879 Left, 892 Right).
  • Tracing the 196,357 outgoing synapses from R1–R8 photoreceptors onto hex-assigned targets anchored 3,936 of 4,107 photoreceptors (95.84%) across 1,486 supported retinal sites (691 L, 795 R), while explicitly zero-masking the remaining 171 unanchored photoreceptors and 285 unsupported hex sites rather than fabricating weights.
  • In native/world-kernels/src/optic_retina.rs and docs/development/BILATERAL_OPTIC_SCREEN.md, OpticRetina attaches left and right compound-eye origins to the live MuJoCo head body pose and casts 1,771 rays per fly (optic_rgb[B, 1771, 3] = 5,313 f32 scalars), intersecting both arena geometry and a physical 3D emissive screen (screen_geom, analytic-vs-MuJoCo raycast distance agreement verified within < 1e-5).

The Bad Apple Paired Screen-Response Experiment (native/webgpu-probe/screen-response.mjs): To prove that visual frames displayed on the physical 3D arena screen propagate through R1–R8 photoreceptors, traverse the 165,122-neuron connectome, and alter MOTOR92 leg/wing actuation in closed loop, Ember ran a paired 600-tick (30.0 s at dt = 0.05 s) rollout starting two embodied flies from byte-identical initial physical and neural states—one facing Bad Apple (site/assets/bad-apple.mp4) on the physical screen (condition: "video") and one facing an unlit black screen (condition: "black") (docs/development/LIVE_CNS_EVIDENCE.md:1-130, site/assets/fly-embodiment-evidence.weave.json):

  • Immediate Photoreceptor & Lamina Divergence: At tick 1, only photoreceptor and first-order optic rows diverged; within ticks 2–10, activity spread through ol_intrinsic, visual_projection, cb_intrinsic, and descending neurons.
  • Whole-CNS Divergence: Over the 600 ticks, 140,200 of 149,782 non-afferent neurons (93.60%) diverged by > 1e-6 (max |Δr| = 0.3168, mean |Δr| = 0.00421).
  • Closed-Loop Motor & Trajectory Divergence: Decoded motor actions diverged on 567 of 600 ticks (94.5%), driving physical 3D root trajectory separation in the MuJoCo habitat.

3.2 Antennal Touch Contact Ledger (6 Massless Collision Proxies)

In standard NeuroMechFly v2.1.0, the antennal segments (pedicel, funiculus, arista) have visual meshes (conntype = 0, contype = 0, conaffinity = 0) that pass through obstacles without generating MuJoCo contact forces. In docs/development/FLY_ANTENNA_TOUCH.md:1-115 and data/body/antenna-contact-proxies-v1.json (commits c9101ae, ef32a32), Ember derived 6 massless collision proxy geoms directly from the vertex clouds of the NeuroMechFly STL meshes:

  • L/R pedicel and L/R funiculus: 95%-coverage principal-axis ellipsoids.
  • L/R arista: Principal-axis capsules with 95th-percentile radial thickness.
  • Integrated at 1000 Hz physics substeps with a 2 ms contact filter time constant, populating bilateral contact-force and slip channels in BODY807.
  • Empirical Verification (B2 Grain Assay): When a free grain strikes the passive left arista, the proxy ledger records a localized force vector of [-0.00372422, -0.00122501, 0.00315742] model-force units and deflects the grain at [8.13465, -2.92297] mm/s, while maintaining byte-exact snapshot/restore determinism across the collision boundary.

3.3 Endogenous Wing-Beat Acoustics (1 kHz Softened Dipole & 16-Band Filterbank)

Rather than treating wing sound as an abstract badge, docs/development/FLY_WING_ACOUSTICS.md:1-120 and native/browser-world/src/fly_acoustics.rs (commits 02203f9, bb28f27) synthesize the physical near-field air-particle velocity generated by the wings at each antenna's Johnston's organ (funiculus midpoint):

  • Relative Wing Centroid Velocity: Subtracting rigid-body root velocity and angular velocity $\mathbf{v}_{\text{rel}} = \mathbf{v}_{\text{wing}} - \left(\mathbf{v}_{\text{root}} + \boldsymbol{\omega}_{\text{root}} \times (\mathbf{x}_{\text{wing}} - \mathbf{x}_{\text{root}})\right)$.
  • Near-Field Softened Dipole Kernel: With wing dipole normal $\mathbf{n}$, softened radius $a = 0.75\text{ mm}$, and gain $G$: $$\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{G \, g \, a^3}{\|\mathbf{r}\|^3 + a^3}\left(3\,\mathbf{n}(\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\text{rel}}) - \mathbf{v}_{\text{rel}}\right)$$
  • 1000 Hz Hann-Windowed Spectral Bank (BODY807[40:62]): Sampled at every 1 ms physics substep into a persisted ring buffer, writing 6 bilateral antenna-local airflow vector components into BODY807[40:46] and 16 log-spaced spectral energy bands (40 Hz to 1600 Hz) into BODY807[46:62]. Because the physical wing actuator bandwidth in MuJoCo has a 400 Hz Nyquist ceiling, the top 4 bands (>= 467.843 Hz) are explicitly zeroed to prevent aliasing artifacts.

3.4 Quasi-Steady Blade-Element Wing Aerodynamics (native/fly-aerodynamics)

In native/fly-aerodynamics/README.md and native/fly-aerodynamics/DESIGN.md:1-110, Ember replaced MuJoCo's built-in ellipsoid fluid approximation with a stateless 24-strip quasi-steady blade-element aerodynamic kernel calibrated to Dickinson, Lehmann & Sane (1999):

  • Mesh-Derived Strip Geometry: Slices the NeuroMechFly l_wing.stl convex hull (span = 2.523 mm, area = 1.841 mm²) into 24 spanwise chords, storing each strip's spanwise center, chord length $c_k$, and leading-to-trailing edge vector.
  • Translational Lift & Drag Coefficients: At every 0.0001 s (10 kHz) MuJoCo substep, evaluates local angle of attack $\alpha_k$ and relative air velocity $\mathbf{U}_k$ at strip $k$, computing: $$C_L(\alpha) = 0.225 + 1.58 \sin(2.13\alpha - 7.2^\circ), \qquad C_D(\alpha) = 1.92 - 1.55 \cos(2.04\alpha - 9.82^\circ)$$ and applying the resulting 3D aerodynamic force and torque vectors directly to L_wing and R_wing via mj_applyFT.

§6. Proof-Carrying Epistemic Hygiene for Computational Biology

A signature architectural contribution of chreatures is the application of cryptographic and state-machine epistemic hygiene—historically reserved for consensus protocols and proof systems—to computational neurobiology.

6.1 The Idempotent Mutation Receipt Protocol (chreatures-request-receipt-v1)

When a long-running evolution or embodiment campaign steps a GPU connectome server over HTTP/IPC (scripts/serve_metal.py, chreatures/neural_client.py), a dropped socket reply on a mutating /step or /reset_state call would ordinarily cause a catastrophic silent divergence: retrying a completed /step double-advances the connectome state (t -> t+2), while skipping an uncompleted /step leaves the brain stale (t).

In tests/test_metal_receipts.py:1-145 and tests/test_neural_receipts.py:1-130, Ember enforced the chreatures-request-receipt-v1 protocol:

  1. Every client session binds a UUID session_id and monotonically increasing request_seq (1, 2, 3, ...) plus a SHA-256 payload_digest in the X-Chreatures-Request-Receipt header.
  2. The Metal connectome server caches the serialized response and post-step state digest for each (session_id, request_seq, payload_digest) tuple:
  3. If a client retries the exact same (session_id, request_seq, payload_digest) after a network timeout, the server replays the cached response without re-stepping the GPU state (replay_count += 1).
  4. If the client sends the same (session_id, request_seq) with a different payload_digest, the server rejects it with HTTP 409 Conflict.
  5. If the client skips a sequence number (request_seq != last_seq + 1), the server rejects it with HTTP 409 Out-of-Order Sequence.
  6. If a socket drops mid-flight and the server cannot verify receipt state on /receipt_status, NeuralClient raises UncertainMutationError and halts the campaign rather than risking corrupted scientific trajectories.

6.2 The Tick-9,967 1-ULP Somatic ATP Exhaustion Discovery (depleted-somatic-payment-v1.receipt.json)

In data/performance/depleted-somatic-payment-v1.receipt.json and docs/SOMATIC_PHYSIOLOGY.md, Ember documented a subtle IEEE-754 floating-point bug that had caused all 64 residents in the long-horizon reef campaign to abort at tick 9,967:

  • When a resident's available_atp drained down to 5.224452869761614e-14 ($5.22 \times 10^{-14}$), the Python/native somatic payment splitter computed:
  • maintenance_paid = 1.9013879491758178e-14
  • activation_paid = 3.323064920585796e-14
  • In exact real arithmetic, the two shares summed to available_atp. In IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic, however, maintenance_paid + activation_paid evaluated to 5.2244528697616146e-14—exceeding available_atp by 1 ULP (6.16e-30) and triggering the strict mass-conservation invariant check total_paid <= available_atp!
  • Resolution & Epistemic Hygiene: In native/resident-runtime, Ember replaced independent proportional rounding with a representably bounded residual subtraction (activation_paid = (available_atp - maintenance_paid).max(0.0).min(requested_activation)), verified across 10,000,000 adversarial subnormal/near-zero IEEE-754 floats in depleted-somatic-payment-v1.receipt.json, while preserving the censored 64-resident campaign artifact unmodified on disk as a permanent forensic record.

6.3 Universal Weave Evidence DAGs (.weave.json)

Across site/assets/fly-embodiment-evidence.weave.json and data/ecology/*.weave.json (built with integrations/weave), every scientific claim is compiled into a typed Directed Acyclic Graph of Claims, Evidence Artifacts (with pinned SHA-256 digests), Verification Tests, Negative Findings, and Explicit Non-Claims (e.g., explicitly stating in fly-embodiment-evidence.weave.json that the Bad Apple assay proves closed-loop retinal$\to$connectome$\to$motor sensitivity, not semantic comprehension of video content, and that MaleCNS + female NeuroMechFly is an explicit cross-sex somatic approximation).

7.1 The 5-Population, 10-ODE Medullary Respiratory CPG (sim/cpg.js)

Following Molkov et al. (2017) and Rubin et al. (2011, J. Comput. Neurosci. 30:607–632), /Users/ember/dev/brorb/sim/cpg.js:1-209 models five ventral respiratory column (VRC) populations using a 10-dimensional state vector y = [V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, hNaP1, hNaP5, mAD2, mAD3, mAD4] (Float64Array(10)):

With firing rate $f_i = \sigma(V_i; k_f = 8.0, V_{h,f} = 0.0) = (1 + e^{-8 V_i})^{-1}$ and fast membrane time constant $\tau_m = 0.02\text{ s}$ (20 ms), the ODE system (sim/cpg.js:124-178) is:

$$\tau_m \frac{dV_i}{dt} = -V_i + I_{\text{intrinsic}, i} + \sum_{j} w_{ij} f_j(V_j) + d_i + d_{i}^{\text{ext}}, \qquad I_{\text{intrinsic}, i} = \begin{cases} g_{\text{NaP}i}\,\sigma(V_i; 10, -0.1)\,h_i & i \in \{1, 5\} \\ -g_{\text{AD}i}\,m_i & i \in \{2, 3, 4\} \end{cases}$$
$$\frac{dh_i}{dt} = \frac{\sigma(V_i; -10.0, -0.2) - h_i}{\tau_{h\text{NaP}}}, \qquad \frac{dm_i}{dt} = \frac{\sigma(V_i; 6.0, 0.1) - m_i}{\tau_{\text{AD}i}}$$

Crucially, biophysical membrane and channel timescales ($\tau_m, \tau_{h\text{NaP}}, \tau_{\text{AD}}$) are strictly invariant (sim/cpg.js:33-39). Respiratory rate is modulated exclusively via tonic drive offsets (driveProfile(targetBpm) in sim/cpg.js:88-95): increasing $d_1$ strengthens pre-BötC inspiratory bursts, decreasing $d_3$ shortens the post-inspiratory pause, and when $\text{targetBpm} > 8.0\text{ BPM}$ ($\text{ratio} > 2.0$), increasing $d_5$ recruits the RTN/pFRG late-E population for active expiration.

7.2 Lung Mechanics, Hering-Breuer Reflex & V/Q-Coupled Chemoreception (sim/lungs.js, sim/chemo.js)

In /Users/ember/dev/brorb/sim/lungs.js:41-76, the 3-state mechanical vector lungY = [ramp_I, x_diaph, v_lung] integrates phrenic motor output (ramp_I, excited by f_preI with $g_{\text{exc}} = 2.0$ and inhibited by f_postI with $g_{\text{inh}} = 3.0$, $\tau_{\text{ramp}} = 0.15\text{ s}$), asymmetric diaphragm contraction/relaxation ($\tau_{\text{contract}} = 0.5\text{ s}$, $\tau_{\text{relax}} = 2.0\text{ s}$), and compliant lung volume ($C = 1.0, R = 0.8$). When v_lung exceeds the pulmonary stretch receptor threshold hb_threshold = 0.85, heringBreuerDrives injects excitatory drive into post-I (+0.3 * psr -> drive_3) and inhibits early-I (-0.15 * psr -> drive_2) to terminate inspiration (the Hering-Breuer inflation reflex).

In /Users/ember/dev/brorb/sim/chemo.js:86-153, blood gas exchange requires both alveolar ventilation ($|\dot{V}_{\text{lung}}|$) and cardiac output perfusion ($\text{effectiveExchange} = \text{ventilation} \times \min(1, \text{CO} / 5.0)$):

  • Arterial & Brain $\text{CO}_2$: $\dot{P}_{a\text{CO}_2} = 0.65 - 0.012 \cdot \text{effectiveExchange} \cdot P_{a\text{CO}_2}$, with brain tissue $P_{\text{CO}_2, \text{central}}$ lagging via $\tau_{\text{central}} = 60.0\text{ s}$ (medullary retrotrapezoid nucleus, RTN, apneic threshold $35.0\text{ mmHg}$) and fast carotid-body $\text{CO}_2$ sensing ($\tau_{\text{peripheral}} = 5.0\text{ s}$).
  • Arterial $\text{O}_2$ & Severinghaus-Hill $\text{SpO}_2$: $\dot{P}_{a\text{O}_2} = 0.008 \cdot \text{effectiveExchange} \cdot (150.0 - P_{a\text{O}_2}) - 0.40$, with oxyhemoglobin saturation: $$\text{SpO}_2 = \frac{P_{a\text{O}_2}^{2.7}}{P_{a\text{O}_2}^{2.7} + 26.8^{2.7}}$$ and a quadratic "hockey-stick" carotid-body hypoxic drive below $P_{a\text{O}_2} = 80.0\text{ mmHg}$ (Marshall 1994).
  • Preventing Apneustic Lockup (chemoCpgDrives, sim/chemo.js:138-153): Routing chemoreceptor drive only to $d_1$ (pre-I/I) would trap the CPG in continuous inspiration (apneusis) during hypercapnia; routing 0.3 * centralDrive + 0.2 * peripheralDrive into $d_3$ (post-I) enables rising $\text{CO}_2$ to break inspiratory lockup and cycle the breath.

7.3 Emergent RSA, Frank-Starling Mechanics, Coronary Ischemia & Acoustic Entrainment

In /Users/ember/dev/brorb/sim/heart.js:165-277, sim/hemodynamics.js:75-127, and sim/autonomic.js:76-103:

  • Emergent Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (RSA): Nucleus Ambiguus Cardiac Vagal Motor Neurons (cvmnActivity, $\tau_{\text{cvmn}} = 0.3\text{ s}$) receive direct synaptic excitation from medullary post-I neurons (+0.15 * fPostI, Gilbey et al. 1984) and inhibition from pre-I/I (-0.25 * fPreI), causing vagal withdrawal and heart-rate acceleration during inspiration followed by vagal restoration and slowing during post-inspiration.
  • Frank-Starling Stroke Volume & Arrhythmia Cascade: Diastolic filling time $t_{\text{fill}} = \max(0.05, 60/\text{HR} - 0.3\text{ s})$ drives preload recruitment $1 - e^{-t_{\text{fill}} / 0.6}$, multiplied by sympathetic/ischemic contractility and afterload penalty. During Ventricular Tachycardia (vt, $\text{HR} \approx 180\text{ bpm}$), $t_{\text{fill}}$ collapses to $0.033\text{ s}$, slashing stroke volume from $70\text{ mL}$ to $\sim 7\text{ mL}$ and cardiac output from $5.0\text{ L/min}$ to $1.3\text{ L/min}$.
  • Closed-Loop Coronary Perfusion & Cerebral Autoregulation: stepHemodynamics computes coronary perfusion pressure as $0.75 \cdot \text{MAP} - \text{LVEDP}$ ($8\text{ mmHg}$). Triggering a myocardial infarction (triggerHeartAttack(0.7)) raises coronary resistance $3.33\times$, decaying ischemiaFactor ($\tau = 8.0\text{ s}$), which depresses contractility, drops MAP, triggers baroreflex sympathetic surge (sympatheticTone > 0.6), and precipitates normal -> vt -> vf -> asystole. Meanwhile, cerebral perfusion remains autoregulated at $1.0$ for $\text{MAP} \in [50, 150]\text{ mmHg}$, ramps down linearly for $\text{MAP} \in [20, 50]\text{ mmHg}$, and scales down brainstem CPG tonic drives (driveScale -> 0) below $20\text{ mmHg}$.
  • AudioWorklet Microphone Breath Entrainment (audio/breath-detector.js:11-90): BreathDetectorProcessor runs in the Web Audio rendering thread with an asymmetric envelope follower ($\tau_{\text{attack}} = 20\text{ ms}$, $\tau_{\text{release}} = 150\text{ ms}$) and online variance tracking ($\text{onsetThresh} = \mu + 2.5\sigma$, $\text{offsetThresh} = \mu + 1.2\sigma$). Upon detecting exhale_start, Simulation.applyBreathEvent injects an excitatory pulse into $d_3$ (post-I), phase-locking the medullary CPG to the human user's exhalation.

8.1 luteastress: Testing Menstrual Synchrony via Exact OU Stressors & Zavala-HPO ODEs

In /Users/ember/dev/luteastress (commits 41b6b96 to f9c6e8f, Feb 8–10, 2026), Ember investigated whether apparent menstrual onset synchrony among cohabitants can arise not from pheromones (critiqued by Yang & Schank 2006), but from shared environmental stressors and shared circadian light schedules acting on the HPA$\to$KNDy$\to$GnRH$\to$ovarian axis.

To test this rigorously at scale, Ember implemented a hybrid Python + Rust/Rayon native extension (luteastress_native in native/src/lib.rs) featuring two distinct models and an exact stochastic stressor generator:

  1. Variance-Preserving Exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Stress Decomposition (native/src/stress.rs:38-135, notes/stress-replacement.md):
  2. Calibrated to Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) perceived-stress autocorrelation ($\text{AR}(1) = 0.277$ at 4h lags $\implies \theta = -\ln(0.277)/(4/24) \approx 7.0\text{ day}^{-1}$, $t_{1/2} \approx 2.2\text{ h}$).
  3. Because $\theta \cdot \Delta t = 7.0 \times 0.25 = 1.75$ violates the Euler-Maruyama stability bound ($\theta \Delta t < 1$), generate_ou_process samples from the exact analytical Ornstein-Uhlenbeck transition distribution: $$S(t + \Delta t) = S(t)\,e^{-\theta \Delta t} + \sigma \sqrt{\frac{1 - e^{-2\theta \Delta t}}{2\theta}}\,\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$
  4. In the treatment arm (shared_fraction $f_s = 0.3$, anchored to Saxbe & Repetti 2010 partner cortisol coregulation $r \in [0.20, 0.30]$), total noise variance $\sigma_{\text{total}}^2 = 0.45^2$ is decomposed into $\sigma_{\text{shared}} = \sigma_{\text{total}}\sqrt{f_s}$ and $\sigma_{\text{indiv}} = \sigma_{\text{total}}\sqrt{1 - f_s}$, guaranteeing that $\text{Var}(S_{\text{shared}} + S_{\text{indiv}}) \equiv \text{Var}(S_{\text{control}})$ so the marginal stress distribution is identical between treatment and control arms!
  1. Model 1: Stochastic Phase-Response Curve (PRC) Oscillator (native/src/cycle.rs:40-170):
  2. Models follicular ($\mu = 14.0\text{ d}, \text{SD} = 3.0\text{ d}$) and luteal ($\mu = 14.0\text{ d}, \text{SD} = 1.5\text{ d}$) phase lengths with $\text{AR}(1)$ cycle-to-cycle autocorrelation ($r = 0.3$).
  3. Following Xiao et al. (1998), stress delays ovulation during the follicular phase via a sigmoid PRC (phase_response_curve) that drops to near zero after ovulation in the luteal phase: $$\text{PRC}(d, L_{\text{foll}}, L_{\text{tot}}) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\left(\frac{d/L_{\text{tot}} - L_{\text{foll}}/L_{\text{tot}}}{0.08}\right)} \cdot \text{clamp}_{[0, 1]}\!\left(\frac{d}{3.0}\right)$$
  1. Model 2: High-Fidelity Zavala (2020) + 54-Hormone HPO Follicle ODE System (native/src/zavala.rs, native/src/mechanistic.rs):
  2. Critical Frequency Bug Fix (notes/zeitgeber-forcing.md:23-39): During development, Ember caught a $24\times$ unit conversion error where $\pi / (24 \times 60)\text{ min}^{-1}$ had been converted to $\pi / 24\text{ day}^{-1}$ (a 24-day circadian period!) instead of $\pi\text{ day}^{-1}$ ($\times 1440\text{ min/day}$), and corrected omega_h0 = PI * 24.0 / 24.2 ($\approx 3.116\text{ rad/day}$ for the $24.2\text{ h}$ human intrinsic circadian period measured by Czeisler et al. 1999 and Duffy et al. 2011).
  3. 6-State Zavala Neuroendocrine Network (ZavalaState): Tracks circadian phase $\phi_H$ with Kuramoto zeitgeber forcing ($K_z = 0.5\text{ day}^{-1}$, derived via phase reduction of the Jewett-Forger-Kronauer 1999 limit-cycle pacemaker), ultradian cortisol phase $\phi_C$ ($\omega_{C0} = 1440\pi/75\text{ day}^{-1}$, $75\text{ min}$ period), quasi-steady amplitude $a_C = \sin^2(\phi_H)(1 + \epsilon s)$, slow genomic cortisol $\tilde{C}$ ($\delta = 7.2\text{ day}^{-1}$), and hypothalamic KNDy neuropeptides Neurokinin B ($N$) and Dynorphin ($D$) driven by estrous skew $f_E(\phi_E) = \sin^2(\phi_E - \sigma \sin^2 \phi_E)$, outputting the KNDy gating factor $f_K \in (0, 1)$ via Hill thresholds ($n = 4, K_s = 0.6, K_c = 1.7$) using unconditionally stable exponential integrators.

  2. Across n_trials = 200 households of 6 cohabitants over 1,095 days (3 years, 90-day burn-in), the Stochastic PRC Model produced negligible phase coherence difference ($\bar{R}_{\text{treat}} = 0.3879$ vs. $\bar{R}_{\text{ctrl}} = 0.3817$, Wilcoxon $p = 0.339$, Cohen's $d = 0.022$), but a highly significant increase in Onset Synchrony Index ($\text{OSI}_{\text{treat}} = 0.2850$ vs. $\text{OSI}_{\text{ctrl}} = 0.2590$, $\Delta\text{OSI} = +0.0260$, Wilcoxon $p = 5.87 \times 10^{-15}$, Cohen's $d = 0.629$)—demonstrating how shared follicular delays create apparent onset clustering without true phase locking.

8.2 febart: The Psychophysics Masterclass & Mathematical Sensory Coding Pipeline

Pedagogical approach: Shannon-style derivations. Don't just state that Weber's Law holds—prove it's the ONLY encoding that satisfies certain constraints."

Gen-1 Clutch (dragons-clutch-dclutch-integration/PROJECT.md) is an exact-integer, fully collateralized outcome-claim protocol on Solana where primitive outcome claims are called Eggs, the market's collateral custody vault is the Hoard, and a market is a Clutch.

2.3 The Five Gen-1 P0 Defects Discovered in ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_2026-08-22.md

Ember's adversarial audit of Gen-1 (archive/gen1/docs/reviews/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_2026-08-22.md) uncovered five structural P0 vulnerabilities that motivated first patching Gen-1 and then launching the clean-sheet dclutch rebuild under COMPOST.md:

  1. ClosePosition Stranded Active Reservations (P0-1): ClosePosition checked only that local PositionAccount cash and Egg balances were zero, without checking ReservationAccount state. An all-in seller whose Eggs were locked in an ACTIVE ReservationAccount could delete their PositionAccount, stranding the reservation and breaking settlement/cancel reclamation. Fixed by adding PositionAccount.open_reservations counter (NonZeroOpenReservations).
  2. CloseGeneralEpoch Epoch Replay & Stranded ClearWork Rent (P0-2): CloseGeneralEpoch closed the Epoch, Window, and funding ledger accounts without advancing a monotone cursor on Market, permitting a closed epoch number to be re-initialized and stranding non-top-3 candidate accounts and 50 KiB ClearWork buffers. Fixed by adding Market.general_epoch_Boundary and CloseRejectedClearWork.
  3. ScoreV1 Complete-Set Wash-Flow Exploit (P0-3): The original batch objective ScoreV1 weighted flow by $p_i (S - p_i) \cdot \text{direct\_flow}_i + \text{distinct\_owners}$. A trader submitting a risk-free complete-set wash trade at a binary midpoint earned $50,000,000q$ score vs $990,000q$ for a real 1% tail trade, allowing a wash trader to outscore real price discovery. Replaced by ScoreV2-Q, which quotients out constant complete-set shifts ($a \mapsto a - (\min_i a_i)\mathbf{1}$) before scoring directional variance.
  4. Unverified Score Claims Evicting Honest Candidates in SealCandidate (P0-4): SealCandidate inserted a solver's claimed score into the top-3 podium before CompleteClearWork verified the stream, allowing a junk candidate with u128::MAX claimed score to evict honest candidates. Fixed by moving podium admission exclusively to CompleteClearWork over the recomputed FullScoreV1.
  5. Necessary-Must-Not-Pose-As-Sufficient Degree-2/3 Moment-Cone Price Gate (P0-5): For degree $d \in \{2, 3\}$ B-splines, interior basis functions never reach $1$ at any evaluation point ($3/4$ ceiling at $d=2$, $2/3$ at $d=3$). Gen-1 V1b checked claimCeiling, butterflyWeight, and single-span Hankel quadrics, which are necessary conditions on the B-spline moment curve but not sufficient for membership in the quantized convex hull $\text{conv}\{\phi(\omega)\}$ across multiple knot spans. This discovery led directly to MomentCone.lean and the constructive sparse 4-atom witness gate (PRICE-GATE-HULL-001, LiabilityBasisV2PriceGate.lean).

2.4 Gen-1 Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean 4 (4,510 Lines), Verus, and Rocq

Gen-1 Clutch contains three distinct formal verification suites under archive/gen1/:

A. Lean 4 Suite (archive/gen1/lean/DragonsClutch/, 9 files, 4,510 lines, zero sorry)

In Solvency.lean, Ember proves that the active collateral requirement $\text{requiredActive}(T) = \max_i T_i$ is the exact supremum over all valid resolution vectors and bounds the ceiling-divided resolved requirement $\text{requiredResolved}(T, v) = \lceil (T \cdot w) / D \rceil$:

lean
theorem P_SOLV_01_resolution_bound (T : List Nat) (v : PayoutVector)
    (hv : v.Valid T.length) :
    requiredResolved T v ≤ requiredActive T := by
  unfold requiredResolved
  apply ceilDiv_le_of_le v.denom_pos
  rw [v.sum_eq]
  exact dot_le_maxList_mul_sum T v.weights hv.1

theorem P_PAY_02_complete_set_liability_exact (n q : Nat) (v : PayoutVector)
    (hv : v.Valid n) :
    liability (List.replicate n q) v = q * v.denominator := by
  unfold liability
  rw [dot_replicate_left q v.weights, hv.2]

In Transitions.lean, P_SOLV_01_resolve_with_vector_admits proves that any active solvent market (m.Solvent, meaning required m ≤ m.hoard) automatically satisfies the prospective post-resolution solvency check for every valid payout vector—proving that the runtime check inside resolveWithVector is pure defense-in-depth and can never refuse a valid resolution:

lean
theorem P_SOLV_01_resolve_with_vector_admits (m : Market) (v : PayoutVector)
    (hphase : m.phase = Phase.active)
    (hsolv : m.Solvent)
    (hv : v.Valid m.totalSupply.length) :
    required { m with phase := Phase.resolved, payout := some v } ≤ m.hoard := by
  have hact : required m = requiredActive m.totalSupply := by
    simp [required, hphase]
  have hres :
      required { m with phase := Phase.resolved, payout := some v } =
        requiredResolved m.totalSupply v := by
    simp [required]
  rw [hres]
  exact Nat.le_trans (P_SOLV_01_resolution_bound m.totalSupply v hv) (hact ▸ hsolv)

In MomentCone.lean, Ember formalizes the exact boundary of the degree-2/3 B-spline moment cone at price scale $S = 8192$, proving both soundness of the ceiling/butterfly certificates and exhibiting the exact interior-peak boundary vector peakedInteriorPrice = [0, 0, 1024, 6144, 1024, 0] where peaked_price_buys_a_nonnegative_payoff_for_less_than_nothing and the_interior_peak_is_the_boundary hold by decide.

B. Verus & Rocq Verification Suites

3.3 Decision 0031 ("The Mechanism Agenda", 2026-09-04): All Six Lean-First Mechanisms

In docs/decisions/0031-the-mechanism-agenda.md (confirmed by Ember on 2026-09-04), six major mechanism extensions were designed Lean-first, proven with zero sorry, and shipped into Cohort 17:

1. Batch Spine (2fbd73474)

Documented in docs/reports/MECHANISM_BATCH_SPINE_2026_09_04.md, scaling batch order clearing to $M = 136$ orders at $3.70\text{ M CU/order}$ across resumable verification pages.

2. Joint Clearing with Checked KKT LP Duality Certificates & Lex-Min Price Canonicality (554a29119)

In JointClearingV1.lean (1,101 lines, 44 theorems, 0 sorry), Ember discharges the standing AGENTS.md rule ("do not say 'optimal clearing' unless an optimality certificate is checked") by requiring every General V1 batch clear to carry a dual KKT certificate Clearing.valid and proving certificate_is_optimal and stranded_supply_is_the_sets_wherever_priced:

lean
theorem certificate_is_optimal (inst : Instance) (c : Clearing) (f : Competitor)
    (hv : c.valid inst) (hf : f.feasible inst) :
    f.surplus inst ≤ c.surplus inst := by
  have h1 : f.surplus inst ≤ c.dualObjective inst :=
    competitor_le_dualObjective inst c f hv.completeSetDual hv.noMinting hf
  have h2 : c.dualObjective inst = c.surplus inst :=
    dualObjective_eq_surplus inst c hv.conservation hv.fillUpper
      hv.inTheMoneyFilled hv.strandedSupplyZero
   omega

To prevent a solver from choosing an arbitrary price vector inside a flat dual-optimal face to favor one side of a limit-tied order, JointClearingV1.lean defines lexMinFrom, an $O(K)$ greedy reduction that drives each coordinate down to its tightest lower bound while preserving $\sum_k p_k = S$, and rejects any non-minimal price vector with RuntimeVerifyErrorV2::NonMinimalPriceVector.

3. Hanson LMSR Scoring-Rule Dealer in Base-2 Q62 Fixed-Point (3bf1905a7)

In ScoringRuleV1.lean (1,390 lines, 0 sorry), Ember formalizes a Hanson Logarithmic Market Scoring Rule automated dealer directly in base-2 fixed-point arithmetic ($W(\text{inv}) = -b \log_2 \sum_i 2^{-\text{inv}_i / b}$) so that $2^x$ and $\log_2$ evaluate via exact integer shift-and-LUT operations without transcendental drift, proving the universal bounded-loss theorem over arbitrary fill sequences:

lean
theorem bounded_loss (P : Potential) (deposit outcomeCount : Nat)
    (fills : List Fill) (i : Nat) (hi : i < outcomeCount)
    (hrun : ∀ f ∈ fills, ...) :
    deposit - (run P (founded P deposit outcomeCount) fills).wealth i ≤
      P.subsidy outcomeCount

On-chain SBF execution of the LMSR dealer measured 39,000 CU ($K=2$), 46,000 CU ($K=3$), and 93,000 CU ($K=5$), compared to 131,790 CU on the selector-9 path.

4. Quorum-Median Ensemble Oracle Resolution (ff4f3b142)

In EnsembleResolutionV1.lean (860 lines, 0 sorry), up to $k \le 5$ declared oracle sources are folded with quorum $q \le k$ using the lower-median order statistic ($\text{rank } \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$). Because cell discretization $x \mapsto \text{cell}(x)$ is monotone, Ember proves the commutation theorem the_cell_of_the_median_is_the_median_of_the_cells, establishing that taking the median in price space and then mapping to outcome cells is identical to mapping each oracle's reading to an outcome cell and taking the median cell.

5. Pro-Rata Founder Bond on Oracle Exhaustion (86d38a203)

In FounderBondV1.lean (682 lines, 34 theorems, 0 sorry), the market founder posts a lamport bond $\text{bondSize} = \text{seatPrepay} + \text{firstCrankShortfall} + \text{ladderFunding}$ (4,031,465 lamports = 0.004031465 SOL on Cohort 15 parameters). If all oracle recovery rungs fail, the bond is walked pro-rata ($\lfloor \text{remaining} \cdot \text{quantity} / \text{outstanding} \rfloor$) to ordinary claim holders, with an_exhausting_walk_pays_the_bond_exactly proving zero stranded lamports when all claims redeem.

6. Conditional (B | A = a) and Product (A × B) Markets (4b15cf69a)

In ConditionalMarketV1.lean (1,056 lines, 50 theorems, 0 sorry), Ember formalizes joint product markets $A \times B$ ($K_A K_B \le 60$, e.g. $7 \times 8 = 56$) and conditional markets $B \mid A = a$ that refund collateral when $A \ne a$, proving:

  • conditional_is_the_row_projection: resolving $A \times B$ and projecting onto row $a$ equals resolving $B \mid A = a$.
  • row_bundle_replicates_the_parent_claim_off_failure: holding one unit of every $B$-branch in row $a$ replicates holding one unit of parent claim $A = a$.
  • branch_claims_pay_nothing_off_condition: if $A$ resolves to $a' \ne a$, every conditional branch claim pays zero and the conditional collateral refunds.

7. Constructive 4-Atom Convex-Hull Price Gate (LiabilityBasisV2PriceGate.lean)

In LiabilityBasisV2PriceGate.lean (754 lines, 0 sorry, transplant PRICE-GATE-HULL-001), Ember closes Gen-1's P0-5 moment-cone sufficiency gap by requiring the solver to supply a constructive 4-atom convex-combination witness (Certificate) from the market's actual payoff table, proving Certificate.price_sum, singleAtom_valid, no_certificate_of_capped_claim, and no_cap_of_attained_scale.

4. degg-research (88 Commits, 03d1ee6): Dark Relation IR, Regulatory Economics, and All 10 Experiments

4.1 Architecture, Privacy Modes, Guarded Holes, and Regulatory Filings

/Users/ember/dev/degg-research (88 commits on main at 03d1ee6, 2026-08-27) is Ember's self-contained cryptographic-economics laboratory for dEgg: a venue where market clearing is compiled to a canonical Dark Relation IR (degg-cbe/v1) and evaluated across three explicit privacy postures defined in docs/PRIVACY_MODES.md and docs/FHE_FRONTIER.md:

  1. Clear: All orders, books, and fills are public; deterministic replay verifies correctness.
  2. ShieldedSingleExecutor: Orders are sealed in commitments ($C = \text{SHA256}(\text{"degg/order/v0"} \parallel \dots)$) and an append-only Merkle Mountain Range (degg-inclusion/v0), hiding intents from the public and competing traders while a single executor computes the batch transition and issues per-owner opening receipts.
  3. DarkThreshold / DarkFHE: No single party sees individual orders; inputs are evaluated under threshold FHE or secret-shared MPC (FHE_FRONTIER.md), opening only the public batch summary $(p^*, V^*)$.

In docs/GUARDED_HOLES_DOSSIER.md, Ember maps the lineage of Guarded Holes (partial turns whose unfilled slots are guarded by algebraic predicates) into dark batch settlement: an order commitment is a guarded hole over the batch state, discharged only when the batch clearing satisfies the owner's limit price, direction, quantity bound, and conservation law.

In docs/regulatory/, the empirical findings of degg-research directly ground four regulatory comment drafts:

  • Prediction Markets ANPRM (CFTC-2026-1717, filed 2026-08-27): Grounded by bundling-invariance and manipulation-cost, proving mathematically that payout-shape rules ("binary vs continuous") are not invariant under complete-set decomposition and quantifying exact constant-product TWAP manipulation costs.

Experiments 2, 3, & 4: dark-fba, dark-fba-independent (300,436,169 Batches), and relation-ir

Freezing the 18-rule deterministic admission check order in DARK_FBA_RELATION.md §4.1 eliminated every divergence, achieving 0 divergences across 300,436,169 enumerated batches:

  • Domain C (82 multi-fault admission perturbations): $\mathbf{551,784}$ batches (0 divergences).
