Experiment 5: inclusion-availability — MMR Commitments, Equivocation Classes, and 7-Class Abort Recovery

experiments/inclusion-availability (131 tests, zero external crates) implements the degg-inclusion/v0 pre-trade commitment log over a FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 Merkle Mountain Range (MMR, verified up to 256 leaves) with leaf hash $H(0\text{x}00 \parallel \text{seq}_{8\text{LE}} \parallel C_{32})$ and peak folding $H(0\text{x}02 \parallel L \parallel R)$. It proves four non-repudiable equivocation classes (ConflictingOrderAtSequence, ConflictingSequenceForCommitment, ConflictingBatchFreeze, and InclusionOmittedFromFreeze), enforces a strict BatchLifecycle state machine (Open -> Frozen -> Settled | Aborted), and closes adversarial audit gap C-1 by adding AbortReason::RelationRefused(BatchRefusalReason) (7 abort classes total) so that a frozen batch whose revealed orders fail dark-fba admission can still deterministically reclaim its deposits via ReclaimTickets.

Experiment 6: shielded-baseline — The 377-of-1,125 Residual Trust Theorem (tests/residual_trust.rs)

experiments/shielded-baseline composes inclusion-availability (Rung 1) with dark-fba (Rung 2), achieving 0 divergences over 90,082 differential test cases (6,561 4-slot + 83,521 5-slot). Crucially, tests/residual_trust.rs asks: Without a ZK computation proof (Rung 5), what can a dishonest single executor forge while still passing all public transcript checks and all 4 per-owner receipt checks?

  • For one fixed admitted batch, residual_trust.rs enumerates 1,125 alternative published runs.
  • 377 of the 1,125 forged runs are accepted by the public verifier and by every individual owner's local check—spanning all 33 well-formed public (clearing_tick, matched_volume) pairs!
  • Why: Each owner checks only that their own fill is consistent with their own limit price and the announced (clearing_tick, matched_volume). Without a Rung-5 proof over the joint order vector, no owner can verify that the announced clearing price actually crossed the other owners' hidden orders.

Experiment 7: settlement-model — How Public Token Transfers Break Dark Matching

experiments/settlement-model (56 tests) implements the 4-state custody lifecycle (Reserved -> Obligated -> Settled | Refunded) with replay-blocking settlement_nullifiers and verifies conservation across all $4! = 24$ claim orders and prefixes. Measuring what an observer learns from token transfers alone across four custody architectures (PerClaimPublic, ShuffledBatchPublic, NettedLedgerInternal, ShieldedNoteModel) proves that under PerClaimPublic, deposit asset type leaks order side (Buy vs Sell) before the batch runs, claim transactions leak slot occupancy and seq rank, and transfer amounts reconstruct the exact seller reservation, exact fill, and narrow a buyer's hidden (limit_tick, quantity) to 2–3 candidates. Only NettedLedgerInternal and ShieldedNoteModel preserve dark-matcher privacy at settlement.

Experiment 8: leakage-lab — Formal Role-Projection Views and the 6-Rule Constant-Shape Dark Budget

experiments/leakage-lab/leakage_lab.py projects any canonical batch scenario across three modes (Clear, Shielded, Dark) and four observer roles (public, executor, owner:<name>, regulator), computing exact field-level visibility (exact, bounded, none) and enforcing the 6-rule Dark disclosure budget: (1) padded 8 × 64B ciphertext slots (512 B constant ingress), (2) single 32B inclusion root, (3) 4-field public output (batch_id, status, clearing_price, total_volume) (zeroing price/volume on refusal), (4) 0 executor plaintext fields in Dark mode, (5) ≤ 2 bounded regulator audit queries (price_conformity, volume_cap), and (6) ≤ 4 constant-size owner fill receipts.

Experiment 9: manipulation-cost — Exact-Integer Constant-Product TWAP Manipulation Laws

experiments/manipulation-cost (1,080 rows in vectors/v1.txt + 8,640 rows in vectors/v2-offhours.txt modeling the stayed NYMEX 24/7 crude oil contract) analyzes the exact integer cost of holding a constant-product pool ($x_0 y_0 = k$, fee $f\text{ bps}$, retention factor $g = \frac{10000 - f}{10000}$) at a target relative move $\delta$ across $k$ of $n$ TWAP buckets (target_shift_bps $= \delta \cdot k / n$):

  • Single-Bucket Exact Round-Trip Cost Formula: Pushing the quote reserve from $y_0$ to $y_0 + d$ and trading back after the sample incurs exact loss: $$c(d) = \frac{(1 - g^2)\, y_0\, d}{y_0 + g^2\, d} \;\le\; y_0 \, \frac{F^2 - (F - f)^2}{(F - f)^2}, \quad F = 10{,}000.$$
  • Three Counter-Intuitive Theorems Established by manipulation-cost:
  • Duration Invariance in Flowless v1: Window length in seconds ($W$) cancels completely from v1 cost; only the bucket count $n$ and hold count $k$ enter.
  • Longer Hold $k$ is Cheaper Without External Arbitrage: For a fixed TWAP shift $S = \delta k / n$, holding the manipulation across more buckets ($k$ larger) requires a smaller per-bucket excursion $\delta = S n / k$; because constant-product slippage is convex in $\delta$, a 1-bucket spike is more expensive than holding a smaller shift across all $n$ buckets when arbitrage flow $r = 0$.
  • Why Independent Per-Bucket Summation Overstates True Attack Cost: When $f > 0$, the swap fee stays inside the pool's reserve and permanently ratchets the invariant $k' > k$ in the attacker's direction, so bucket $2..k$ require less trade input than bucket $1$!
  • Off-Hours Liquidity Thinning (vectors/v2-offhours.txt): When off-hours liquidity drops by ratios $1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/10, 1/50$, a settlement window wholly inside the thin session loses manipulation resistance linearly (10000, 5003, 2501, 1004, 203 bps), whereas a 12-bucket window spanning only 2 thin buckets claws back $6\times$ the cost (59776, 29889, 14946, 5980, 1200 bps).

Experiment 10: confidential-energy-dispatch (p3-t3-b2-q4/v0) — Nonconvex Unit Commitment in RelationModule

In research/confidential-energy-dispatch (commit 08a0fc3, 25 tests, CONFIDENTIAL_ENERGY_DISPATCH_RELATION.md), Ember proves that degg-relation-ir generalizes beyond financial auctions to confidential physical infrastructure clearing:

  • Model: 3 padded generators (0..2), 3 periods (0..2), 2 buses joined by a lossless line of capacity $C \in \{0..12\}$, integer outputs $q_{i,t} \in \{0..4\}$, nonconvex minimum-output when committed ($q_{\min} \le q_{i,t} \le q_{\max}$), startup cost, ramp-up/ramp-down bounds ($|q_{i,t} - q_{i,t-1}| \le R$), forced-outage ramp-down bypass when $q_{\max,i,t} = 0$, and 2-segment piecewise marginal costs.
  • Canonical Optimum Selection: Over the reference benchmark (demands = [[3,2], [2,3], [2,2]], line_cap = 1), the solver explores 8,025 first-two-provider trajectory pairs, identifies 468 feasible schedules, selects the unique lexicographically smallest minimum-cost schedule outputs = [[2,2,2], [1,3,2], [2,0,2]] with total_cost = 56 and provider credits [18, 30, 8], and rejects a feasible, conserving, recommitted schedule ([[1,2,1], [2,3,3], [2,0,2]], total_cost = 60) with RefusalClass::NotCanonicalOptimum.

5.2 sol-misc/passwap (22e64cf) & dregg-otc: Verus-Verified Passphrase OTC Escrow on Solana Mainnet

/Users/ember/dev/dregg-otc (program/src/lib.rs, 419 lines of raw solana-program 3.0) was Ember's first passphrase-claimable Solana OTC escrow prototype, where a maker deposits token A and records an Ed25519 claim_key derived client-side from a shared passphrase via PBKDF2-SHA512 (600,000 rounds, salt "dregg-otc/v1/" || offer_address). Because the claimer signs the Take transaction with claim_key and their own wallet payer, the passphrase never touches the blockchain and cannot be mempool-sniped.

In /Users/ember/dev/sol-misc/passwap (HEAD 22e64cf), Ember re-engineered this design into passwap, a formally verified, non-custodial protocol deployed immutable (upgrade authority: none since 2026-09-26) on Solana Mainnet at 7bGfrNxemPSvthXXnYcHfDY8cjgWYeeysWm463tzfmh6 (72,240-byte programdata, SHA-256 fd5014de8911ab4859bd55b7240defac040ec7ebd945bcd43cf8e656b19271bc built from commit e9cb50e):

  • 2-of-3 SPL Multisig Custody (P12, P13, P15): Unlike dregg-otc (where the Offer PDA owned the vault alone), a passwap vault is owned by an SPL Token 2-of-3 multisig of [offer PDA, maker, claim_key]. The program can never move a vault on its own signature (no_vault_moves_on_the_programs_signature_alone), and maker + claimer hold 2 of the 3 keys (the_parties_hold_two_of_three_keys), so they can recover funds via raw SPL Token instructions even if the passwap program is closed or bypassed!
  • Partial Takes, Free Offers (amount_b == 0), Vault Top-Ups, and $DREGG Fee Routing:
  • make charges a flat 1,000 DREGG (MAKE_FEE = 1_000_000_000 at 6 decimals, mint XkeTXo1125vz5H9svJpGiw4JvLbN8VmMu9cmMvspump).
  • take admits any partial fill 0 < take_a <= vault.amount paying pay_b that clears the oriented cross-multiplied rate in u128: pay_b * amount_a >= amount_b * take_a, plus an 0.088% take fee (pay_b * 88 / 100_000), or pay_b == 0 with zero token-B accounts for a free offer (amount_b == 0).
  • Verus Proof Suite (passwap/core/src/lib.rs, 77 verified items, 0 errors, 17 named theorems in PROPERTIES.md):
  • Pure #![no_std], allocator-free core inside verus! { ... } paired with a 330-line pinocchio SBF adapter (passwap/program/src/lib.rs).
  • Every decision function (decide_make, decide_take, decide_cancel) carries a two-sided specification (None ==> !*_conditions(f) completeness; Some(p) ==> *_conditions(f) && *_plan_is(f, &p) soundness) plus exact per-key signed balance-delta conservation theorems (theorem_make_effect, theorem_take_effect, theorem_free_take_effect, theorem_cancel_effect):
rust
/// P12. The program never moves a vault on its own signature: every vault move is by the 2-of-3 multisig,
/// with the offer PDA as one signer and the claimer (take) or the maker (cancel) as the other.
pub proof fn no_vault_moves_on_the_programs_signature_alone(t: &TakeFacts, tp: &TakePlan, c: &CancelFacts, cp: &CancelPlan)
    requires take_conditions(t), take_plan_is(t, tp), cancel_conditions(c), cancel_plan_is(c, cp)
    ensures
        tp.release.multisig && tp.release.authority@ == t.vault_auth.key@ && tp.release.pda@ == t.offer.key@ && tp.release.cosigner@ == t.claim.key@,
        t.vault_auth.head@[0] == 2 && t.vault_auth.head@[1] == 3,
        cp.refund.multisig && cp.refund.authority@ == c.vault_auth.key@ && cp.refund.pda@ == c.offer.key@ && cp.refund.cosigner@ == c.maker.key@,
        c.vault_auth.head@[0] == 2 && c.vault_auth.head@[1] == 3 {}

1.2 fn1 Architecture, Engineering Laws & Core Theorems

As specified in AGENTS.md and docs/architecture.md, fn1 is governed by five non-negotiable engineering laws:

  1. ACL2 Owns Every Decision: Protocol framing, RFC 3977 command parsing, RFC 5322/5536 article validation, Cancel-Lock (RFC 8315), store admission, retention, BPv7 bundle framing (RFC 9171), BPSec (RFC 9172), TCPCLv4 (RFC 9174), and store-node state transitions live inside certified ACL2 books with :verify-guards t.
  2. Guard-Verified *1* Execution: In host/interfaces.lisp, the SBCL host invokes ACL2's compiled *1* executable counterparts (ACL2_*1*_ACL2::<FN>) only after asserting input guards on the Lisp boundary (assert-guard), so runtime execution runs raw compiled SBCL without interpreter overhead.
  3. Three-Valued Durable Outcome (accepted / refused / uncertain): Every durable mutation distinguishes pre-commit refusal from post-write crash uncertainty.
  4. D27 Concrete Representation Discipline: Octet lists (fn-b3-octet-listp) are the logical specification model only; concrete articles and indices stay in compact byte arrays / stobj carriers outside the logical bridge, reducing in-use SBCL heap after 1,000 posts to 68 MiB.
  5. FFI vs. Verified-In-Logic Cryptography: Ed25519 (crypto_sign_ed25519_verify_detached), SHA-256/512, Argon2id, and PQClean ML-DSA-65 (host/native/fn-mldsa65.c) cross a narrow 5-function C FFI seam, while BLAKE3 is formalized directly in ACL2 in books/blake3.lisp and proven 32-octet shape-preserving across unkeyed, keyed, and key-derivation modes:
lisp
;; /Users/ember/dev/fn/books/blake3.lisp:311-339
(defthm fn-b3-hash-shape
  (and (fn-b3-octet-listp (fn-b3-hash key flags octets))
       (true-listp (fn-b3-hash key flags octets))
       (equal (len (fn-b3-hash key flags octets)) 32)))

(defthm fn-blake3-shape
  (and (fn-b3-octet-listp (fn-blake3 m))
       (true-listp (fn-blake3 m))
       (equal (len (fn-blake3 m)) 32)))

(defthm fn-blake3-of-octets
  (implies (fn-b3-octet-listp m)
           (equal (fn-blake3 m) (fn-b3-hash *fn-b3-iv* 0 m))))

In books/store-node.lisp, the 14-slot v6 store-node record (fn-sn-make-v6) separates hot served queries (fn-sn-statement-lookup, fn-sn-equivocatorp, fn-sn-verdict-lookup) from the underlying article store (fn-stx-store) so that serving a statement or equivocation check never walks the store or re-parses an article, while enforcing strict rule-hygiene (tools/rule_cost.py) by disabling constructor/projection definitions on export. During fn's crash-cut testing on OpenBSD 7.9 FFS2, Ember's durability harness also uncovered a real OpenBSD 7.9 FFS2 fsck bug where fsck deleted already-fsynced files after a simulated power cut.

1.3 fn2 (/Users/ember/dev/fn/fn2): Bottom-Up Rebuild as a General Persistent Event Log

Launched on 2026-10-28 (fn2/docs/design/FN2-ORIENTATION.md) and reaching 413 commits in 72 hours (fn2/docs/design/CONVERGENCE-20261031.md), /Users/ember/dev/fn/fn2 rebuilds fn from the ground up as a general persistent event log for Robigalia/Dregg (E0–E4), where NNTP (Layer D, serving 14 verbs at df9be72b5) is just one projection port over an append-only ordered-run storage engine:

  • Declaration Macro DSLs:
  • fn2/books/columns.lisp (defcolumns): Declares typed columnar stobj/alist tables with automatic frame theorems (update-col-i preserves col-j for $i \neq j$).
  • fn2/books/machines.lisp & fn2/books/machine-arms.lisp (defmachine with the G3 child-form step language): Compiles declarative machine arms over 11 step verbs (:do, :set, :next, :case, :issue, :park, :charge, :stop, :repeat, :goto, :wake-row) into both guard-verified ACL2 transition functions and inspectable metadata tables (*<name>-arms*).
  • fn2/books/arms.lisp (defcost) & fn2/books/squares.lisp (defsquare): Binds step budgets and refinement squares directly at declaration time.
  • Layers A–H:
  • Layer A (pool, scheduler, executor): Bounded resource pools, work-conserving coroutine scheduler, and non-blocking I/O step dispatch.
  • Layer B (crash, log, commit, allocator): Write-ahead log, durable commit barrier, and crash-cut recovery.
  • Layer C (ordered-run, ribbon, overlay, C5 sealer): Ordered-run engine with Ribbon filters and the C5 size-tiered sealer compaction merge (c5-sealer), proven order-preserving and key-lookup invariant.

1.4 fn2/meta: The 62,742-LOC Lean 4 Metatheory & 2,705-Function Shallow Embedding

Because ACL2 is first-order and cannot quantify over relations, machine kinds, or refinement squares, /Users/ember/dev/fn/fn2/meta embeds both the metatheory and the actual fn2 ACL2 world into Lean 4 (v4.29.0-rc2 + Mathlib):

  1. Thin Double Category of Refinement Squares (Fn2/Square.lean): Formalizes simulation squares over RelCat where Sq v₀ v₁ h₀ h₁ states $\forall a\,b\,c,\; v_0\,a\,b \to h_0\,a\,c \to \exists d,\; h_1\,b\,d \wedge v_1\,c\,d$, with horizontal pasting (Sq.seq), vertical stacking (Sq.stack), 4-square pasting (Sq.paste), and the adequacy theorem Sq.paste_cover showing horizontal composition of Covers (∀ c a, v₀ a c → ∃ b, v₀ a b ∧ h₀ a b) is a Covers.
  2. Mazurkiewicz Trace Coherence & Negative Teeth (Fn2/Coherence.lean): Proves Fn2.Coherence.coherence (permuting independent steps preserves reachability) and footprint_independent (disjoint read/write column footprints commute), paired with negative teeth acceptClose_without_g2, acceptClose_not_diamond, and liar_not_diamond proving that omitting the G2 guard or lying about footprints breaks the diamond property.
  3. Revision Conservativity (Fn2/Conservative.lean) & Representation Parametricity (Fn2/Param.lean): Proves Fn2.Conservative.conservative and Fn2.Param.abstraction (plus negative tooth peek_breaks_abstraction).
  4. Shallow Embedding of 2,705 ACL2 Functions & 1,576-Call 4-Way Equivalence (Fn2/Instances/LayerAWorld.lean, Fn2/Pathway.lean): Via fn2/tools/print-world.lisp and fn2/meta/scripts/emit_embed.py, the entire closed ACL2 world of fn2 (2,705 ACL2 functions, 2,089 stated guards, 15 machine kinds of which 8 are in G3 child form, and 68 declared operations) is emitted into Lean 4 over Fn2.ACL2.Val (LayerAWorld.lean: 26,342 lines; LayerA.lean: 19,081 lines; LayerAEqns1..4.lean: 4,155 rfl binary-search-tree dispatch equations). Running lake exe fn2-measure verified 100% 4-way agreement across (a) the independent Lean step interpreter Fn2.Arms.runArm, (b) the generated ACL2 transition function, (c) the guard predicate, and (d) the column frame condition on 963/963 echo+scribe calls, 582/582 cursor calls, and 31/31 meta-probe calls (1,576/1,576 total), catching 2 G3 generator defects and 2 interpreter defects before setting up Fn2.Pathway.ArmCorrect and KindCorrect (PW1–PW5b) to replace ATC C-from-ACL2 with a Lean-native C emission pipeline.
lean
-- /Users/ember/dev/fn/fn2/meta/Fn2/Square.lean:38-77
def Sq {A B C D : Type u}
    (v₀ : RelCat.Hom A B) (v₁ : RelCat.Hom C D)
    (h₀ : RelCat.Hom A C) (h₁ : RelCat.Hom B D) : Prop :=
  (h₀ ≫ v₁).rel ≤ (v₀ ≫ h₁).rel

theorem Sq.paste
    (s₀₀ : Sq v₀ v₁ h₀₀ h₁₀) (s₀₁ : Sq v₁ v₂ h₀₁ h₁₁)
    (s₁₀ : Sq v₀' v₁' h₁₀ h₂₀) (s₁₁ : Sq v₁' v₂' h₁₁ h₂₁) :
    Sq (v₀ ≫ v₀') (v₂ ≫ v₂') (h₀₀ ≫ h₀₁) (h₂₀ ≫ h₂₁) :=
  Sq.stack (Sq.seq s₀₀ s₀₁) (Sq.seq s₁₀ s₁₁)

2.1.1 Empirical & Mechanistic Audit of jesse.my (/Users/ember/dev/jesse-notes)

In /Users/ember/dev/jesse-notes/BENCH.md and HANDOFF.md, Ember evaluated Andy's live https://jesse.my model across 617 held-out items spanning 8 Oracle7 specialist panels (acoustics, cooking-v3, densities, units, units-v3, springs, fluids, fuels) using bench/jesse.py, bench/jesse_report.py, and bench/jesse_mechinterp.py:

  • Under verified-only scoring (treating verified: false as abstention), jesse.my scored 29 ok / 128 wrong / 458 withheld / 2 false-yes.
  • Re-scoring with bench/jesse_report.py (extracting the first numeric token to forgive unit-wording variations) showed 114 of the 128 "wrong" items actually contained the right number, leaving 14 genuine misread-question errors that still carried verified: true—such as adding decibels linearly (70 dB + 65 dB = 135 instead of $10 \log_{10}(10^7 + 10^{6.5}) \approx 71.19\text{ dB}$), using the wrong density table row, or inverting a unit ratio.
  • Pulling 20 6-stage internal traces from /api/v1/mechinterp via bench/jesse_mechinterp.py proved that verified: true only certified that the arithmetic inside jesse's Python sandbox ran without throwing an exception—not that the selected formula or context premise matched the question.

  • Verified Multi-Organ Arbitration (src/isabelle/Arbitration.thy): Formalizes candidate ranking so that a checked context-mismatch refusal (Refusal CheckedContextRefusal) strictly defeats an unverified or tied answer (checked_context_refusal_wins_tie), preventing the jesse.my failure mode where a fluent wrong-formula calculation overrides a specialist refusal:
isabelle
(* /Users/ember/dev/o7vn/src/isabelle/Arbitration.thy:86-118 *)
datatype refusal_kind = CheckedContextRefusal | UncheckedRefusal
datatype candidate_kind = VerifiedAnswer | Refusal refusal_kind | UnverifiedAnswer

fun kind_rank :: "candidate_kind \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "kind_rank (Refusal CheckedContextRefusal) = 3"
| "kind_rank VerifiedAnswer = 2"
| "kind_rank (Refusal UncheckedRefusal) = 1"
| "kind_rank UnverifiedAnswer = 0"

theorem checked_context_refusal_wins_tie:
  assumes "kind c1 = Refusal CheckedContextRefusal"
      and "kind c2 = VerifiedAnswer"
      and "score c1 = score c2"
  shows "better_candidate c1 c2"
  using assms by (simp add: better_candidate_def)
  • Verified Relation Reader (src/isabelle/Relation_Reader.thy, Relation_Reader_Export.thy, Relation_Reader_Test.thy): Proves 18 theorems over schema-typed relational projections, joins, and unit-aware lookups, kernel-checked against 8 real SQLite fixtures in Relation_Reader_Test.thy.

2.3 /Users/ember/dev/svenvs — Self-Verifying & Self-Improving Prover/Compiler Environments in HOL4 & CakeML

Spanning 90 commits from 2026-05-15 to 06f03eb (2026-11-01) across 21 HOL4 *Script.sml theories (0 cheats), /Users/ember/dev/svenvs (Self-Verifying Environments; see ARCHITECTURE.md) answers a foundational question in formal methods and AI safety: How can a running agent weaken its safety policy, upgrade its own theorem prover, and hot-swap its own native compiler in-place without ever violating its root safety invariant or falling into Löb's theorem circularity?

svenvs resolves this through six proved HOL4 pillars:

  1. Runtime Shielding (safetyScript.sml): Defines shielded_step policy fallback s a and proves safety_preservation: if policy and fallback preserve Safe, then any untrusted action stream acts executed through shielded_run remains inside Safe for all $t \in \mathbb{N}$.
  2. Safe Policy Weakening & Monotone Authority Expansion (sv_weakeningScript.sml): Proves that an agent can replace its runtime shield p_old with a strictly more permissive shield p_new (weaker p_old p_new $\equiv \forall s\,a,\; p_{\text{old}}\,s\,a \Rightarrow p_{\text{new}}\,s\,a$) provided it first discharges a proof obligation preserves_safe env p_new. Proves safe_weakening, authority_monotone, and the necessity tooth safe_weakening_needs_weaker.
  3. Finite Watchdog Discharge vs. Löb Obstruction (kernel/watchdogFiniteScript.sml, kernel/loebReduction/loebReductionScript.sml):
  4. In watchdogFiniteScript.sml, proves loeb_finite_obstruction (a system cannot prove its own unbounded soundness without a stronger assumption) alongside wd_encodes_obligation, showing that a bounded horizon watchdog ($N$-step safety certificate) can be discharged inside the base theory without invoking Large Cardinal Axioms (LCA).
  5. In loebReductionScript.sml, uses HOL4's fast kernel compute engine (cv_eval) to verify initial HOL context syntax (init_ctxt_syntax_cv_verified) and proves lca_encodes_soundness for unbounded reflection.
  6. Concrete Candle Self-Prover Upgrade (selfproverConcrete/selfProverConcreteScript.sml): Instantiates the abstract self-prover over Candle (the verified HOL prover inside CakeML), proving frozen_checker_sound_candle and prover_self_improvement_is_safe_candle: an untrusted heuristic prover fast_prover can be upgraded arbitrarily so long as its proof objects pass the frozen kernel checker check_thm.

Per-Generation In-Place CakeML Compiler Self-Upgrade (selfUpgrade/evalUpgradeBScript.sml, evalUpgradeOpScript.sml, selfUpgradeEndToEndScript.sml, selfUpgradeMultiSwapScript.sml): Extends CakeML's Eval oracle state with a generation-indexed compiler record (do_eval_record_gen_def) and proves swap_preserves_recorded_orac_wf_gen and multi_swap_sound: the running system can hot-swap its own compiler $C_0 \to C_1 \to \dots \to C_k$ across arbitrarily many generations while preserving recorded_orac_wf_gen.

3.2 The 9 HOL4 Theories (hol/stella*Script.sml): Mechanizing Boris Eng's Exegesis

Every definition and theorem number in hol/ is cross-indexed directly to Boris Eng's An Exegesis of Transcendental Syntax:

  1. hol/stellaTermScript.sml & hol/stellaPolarisedScript.sml: Defines first-order stellar terms, variable renaming/disjointness, polarised rays (+, -, neutral), and constellations.

3.3 Core Theoretical Contributions in stella-core: Reafferent Closure, Proper Time & The Kruskal Whistle

Inside crates/stella-core/src/ (52 Rust modules), Ember translates the HOL4 semantics into a high-speed engine and resolves three foundational problems in synthetic agency (HISTORY.md, HISTORY-2026-05-17.md):

  1. Reafferent Closure vs. Bare Operational Closure (crates/stella-core/src/reafference.rs): Ember raised the "gut microbiome" objection against bare Maturana/Varela operational closure: any catalytically closed sub-soup inside a larger constellation would trivially count as an "individual" even if it never acts upon or senses an external world. reafference.rs defines individuation as a reafferent fixed point that crosses the agent/environment cut twice ($A \xrightarrow{\text{effector}} E \xrightarrow{\text{sensor}} A$), requiring motor-to-sensory mutual information and counterfactual action sensitivity above sham-cut controls.
  2. Proper Time vs. Substrate Clock & The "Invariant => Flat" Viability Law (crates/stella-core/src/valence.rs): Distinguishes the external simulation step counter $t_{\text{substrate}}$ from the organism's internal proper time $\tau$ (counted in completed reafferent fusion cycles). Furthermore, valence.rs proves the "invariant $\Rightarrow$ flat" dilemma: any quantity that is strictly conserved under all transitions has a zero gradient everywhere and therefore cannot serve as a viability/steering signal; valence must be defined over a metabolically dissipating homeostatic reserve that can actually be lost.

The centerpiece mechanistic experiment of h is research/results/anatomy/summary.md (commits 5ae5aaf, 85bb541), which asks: When a hybrid Mamba2/Transformer model undergoes full-weight continued pretraining into a room resident, which parameter group (attention, mamba, mlp, embeddings, norms) actually carries the new voice, and which causes benchmark forgetting?

Ember constructed 12 surgical hybrid checkpoints over Falcon-H1-0.5B: the untouched base model, the full CPT resident (h-05b-replay), 5 only-G models (base weights everywhere except group $G$ transplanted from resident), and 5 allbut-G models (resident weights everywhere except group $G$ reverted to base):

This 12-way intervention established two non-obvious laws of hybrid Mamba/Transformer adaptation:

  1. Voice and Discourse Cadence Localize to the Mamba2 SSM Mixer: Transplanting only-mamba alone captures 32.3% of the library loss reduction and 34.4% of the room loss reduction, while reverting Mamba to base (allbut-mamba) destroys 63.1% of the library adaptation and collapses the model's multi-sentence literary voice back into short base completions.
  2. The Weight-Movement Paradox (attention Moves Hardest in L2 Yet Is Causally Disposable): In parameter space, attention moved the most of any module (0.28097 relative L2 norm), which would naively suggest attention is where adaptation happens or that freezing attention would prevent capability drift. Yet only-attention captures almost nothing (4.6% lib / 6.1% room), and reverting all 36 layers of attention to base (allbut-attention) leaves the resident's book-voice intact and changes the audit score by 0.001 (0.525 $\to$ 0.524). Furthermore, State Recall with Segment Masking (research/staterecall/README.md, research/s0/README.md) proved that blocking cross-segment attention forces passage information through the Mamba recurrent state, improving semantic recognition from 0.59 (unmasked, where attention acts as a lazy 16-gram surface copier 0.29 $\to$ 0.90) to 0.82 (masked), whereas on the plain-transformer control K2-0.9B, segment masking drops question-logit sensitivity to the passage to identically 0.

Across what superficially appear to be five disparate creative domains—(1) rotating-frame zero-gravity sports (spindle), (2) binary-oracle RTS reconstruction and Lean 4 formal board games (don, automatafl, webapp2-auto), (3) tactical/aerodynamic/retrocausal game engines (bw-exp0, bw-exp1, blackwing-v0, frisqueendom, friskingdom, resequence-rs, Achron, booty-hunt, booty-haul, megastructure-maintenance-crew, pinatatown, esgea, multiway-tug, tictacflicflacfloe, path-of-angels), (4) reverse DAWs, programmatic synthesis, and beat-locked video composition (audec, audec-wt, audec-ui-platform-probe, kitforge, vidbox, scrubsheet, codrawer-bridge), and (5) multiphysics nuclear criticality and reactor simulators (plymouth-rock, buckeye)—Ember's engineering exhibits a single, unmistakable structural signature:

  1. Mechanics Derived From First-Principles Physics, Never Decorated: Whether deriving the entire rulebook and stadium economy of an interstellar sport from the confluent root $\lambda = -i\omega$ of the rotating-frame Coriolis/centrifugal ODE (spindle), computing Ultimate Frisbee stall falloff and gyroscopic pitching moments from $C_L(\alpha)$ and $C_m(\alpha)$ curves (frisqueendom, friskingdom), modeling Caribbean piracy as a continuous-time sweep-width and horizon-geometry arms race (booty-haul), or coupling 6-group Pu-239 delayed-neutron point kinetics to 1D liquid-sodium Dittus-Boelter thermal channels and 2 GWh molten-salt tanks (plymouth-rock), gameplay and simulation behavior emerge strictly from integrating real physical conservation laws.

The Zero-Twin & Differential Oracle Doctrine: Wherever a specification exists—whether a shipped 2003 x86 executable (riseofnations.exe in don), a 2011 retrocausal RTS binary (Achron in resequence-rs), or a formal board-game ruleset (automatafl)—Ember refuses to allow two unverified implementations to drift apart. In automatafl, the Rust server and WASM client contain zero game-rule code: Lean 4 (lean/Automatafl/*.lean) compiles to C IR and links directly into native and WASM binaries (Zero-Twin architecture). In don, the Rust simulation is held against an in-process 32-bit x86 fork-isolated binary oracle (crates/oracle) across 18,722,565 differential trials with zero mismatches and a DataWalk byte-image container (crates/don-state) that reproduces all 15 retail lockstep Adler-32 checksum channels.

Abelian / Tropical Determinism on CPU and GPU: Floating-point non-associativity and thread-scheduling races are systematically eliminated at the algebraic level. don-gpu implements batched pathfinding relaxation in WGSL (flowfield.wgsl) using exclusively u32 min-plus tropical arithmetic ($\min(d, \text{neighbour} + w)$) with 8×8 temporal blocking in workgroup memory and resolves many-to-one entity interactions via segmented reductions over the abelian group $\mathbb{Z}/2^{32}\mathbb{Z}$ (reduce.rs) rather than hardware atomics. spindle locks its 240 Hz RK4 integrator and sfc32 PRNG substreams to bit-identical f64 constants between Rust/WASM and TypeScript (FRICTION_DECAY = 0.9753099120283326).

1. spindle — SPINDLE · RIG: Zero-Gravity Rotating-Frame Sport & Dynamical Systems Engine

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/spindle (git@github.com:emberian/spindle.git, 162 commits through 2ad529c on 2026-05-20).

1.1 The Physical & Worldbuilding Substrate: "The Room the Universe Already Built"

In README.md and design/sport.md, Ember defines RIG (Formal league name: the Spindle League), a zero-gravity sport played along the weightless central axis ("the calm") of rotating O'Neill cylinders in the 25th-century Vivere Astra campaign setting. Rather than inventing sci-fi rules and decorating them with zero-gravity visuals, every mechanic of RIG is mathematically derived from three physical invariants of a rotating cylinder (design/sport.md):

  1. Centrifugal Slope ("Deep is faithful, high is free"): Effective gravity scales linearly with cylindrical radius $\rho = \sqrt{y^2 + z^2}$ via $g(\rho) = \omega^2 \rho$. At $\rho = 0$ (the spine), players and the ball are weightless; dropping rimward toward the boundary skin ($R = 45.0\,\text{m}$) buys speed and heavy momentum at the cost of reversibility.
  2. **Chiral Handedness (Spinward Faith vs. Antispinward Free): Because the habitat rotates at angular velocity $\vec{\omega} = \omega \hat{x}$, the Coriolis acceleration $-2\vec{\omega} \times \vec{v}$ breaks reflection symmetry. Throwing spinward produces a familiar downward-curving arc (Fall, worth 2 points through the Faith ring); throwing antispinward against the habitat's rotation lifts the projectile inward across the axis (Rise, worth 3 points through the Free ring, or 4 points for a Curl with $\ge \pi/2$ cross-sectional turn, or 6 points for a closed self-returning Loop** with $\ge 2.2\,\text{rad}$ turn).
  3. Grapple-Only Locomotion: In vacuum/weightlessness, players cannot swim or walk in mid-air; they can only alter their velocity by pushing off solid structure (pushoff), firing a powered winch-and-claw tether (rig line) at structural spars or other players, or firing micro-thrusters (thrumbler).

The sport syntheses American football's territorial downs (a Cast: 3 throws to advance past the next axial gate) with baseball's clockless, stat-haunted 1-on-1 duels (a Contest: when a defender challenges a bell in flight within CONTEST_RADIUS = 6.0 m, play freezes into a 3-exchange count between thrower and contester) over nine clockless innings (design/sport.md). Even the ball—the bell—is derived from the setting: it contains an internal mass-ring that chimes cleanly when spinning on its principal axis and clatters disharmonically when knocked off-axis, allowing matches to be followed by ear over low-bandwidth interstellar jump-delayed "re-calls" (league/teams.md).

1.2 Rotating-Frame Roulette Mechanics & Analytical Trajectory Solver

In game/rig-core/src/trajectory.rs, the cylinder's long axis is $+x$, and the cross-section is $(y, z)$ rotating with angular velocity $\vec{\omega} = (\omega, 0, 0)$. Combining the centrifugal acceleration $-\vec{\omega} \times (\vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}) = (0, \omega^2 y, \omega^2 z)$ and the Coriolis acceleration $-2\vec{\omega} \times \vec{v} = (0, 2\omega v_z, -2\omega v_y)$ yields the exact equations of motion:

$$\ddot{x} = 0, \qquad \ddot{y} = \omega^2 y + 2\omega \dot{z}, \qquad \ddot{z} = \omega^2 z - 2\omega \dot{y}$$

Writing the cross-sectional position as a complex number $\zeta(t) = y(t) + i z(t)$, the $(y,z)$ system collapses into the scalar complex second-order ODE:

$$\ddot{\zeta} + 2i\omega\dot{\zeta} - \omega^2\zeta = 0 \implies (\partial_t + i\omega)^2 \zeta = 0$$

Because the characteristic polynomial $(\lambda + i\omega)^2 = 0$ has a double confluent root $\lambda = -i\omega$, every free-flight trajectory in the calm is an exact two-term roulette (game/rig-core/src/trajectory.rs):

rust
// /Users/ember/dev/spindle/game/rig-core/src/trajectory.rs (lines 18-65)
/// Total acceleration in the rotating frame (Coriolis + centrifugal).
///   a_x = 0
///   a_y =  2·ω·vz + ω²·y
///   a_z = -2·ω·vy + ω²·z
#[inline]
pub fn accel(p: Vec3, v: Vec3, omega: f64) -> Vec3 {
    let w2 = omega * omega;
    Vec3::new(
        0.0,
        2.0 * omega * v.z + w2 * p.y,
        -2.0 * omega * v.y + w2 * p.z,
    )
}

/// Closed-form solution of the rotating-frame EOM at time `t` from `(p0, v0)`.
///
/// Write ζ = y + i·z.  Then  ζ̈ + 2iω ζ̇ − ω² ζ = 0  has double root −iω, so
///   ζ(t) = (A + B·t) · e^(−iωt),   A = ζ₀,  B = ζ̇₀ + iω·ζ₀.
pub fn analytic(p0: Vec3, v0: Vec3, omega: f64, t: f64) -> PointState {
    let x = p0.x + v0.x * t;
    let vx = v0.x;

    // A = (ay, az),  B = (by, bz) = (vy0 - ω·z0, vz0 + ω·y0)
    let ay = p0.y;
    let az = p0.z;
    let by = v0.y - omega * p0.z;
    let bz = v0.z + omega * p0.y;

    // u(t) = A + B·t
    let uy = ay + by * t;
    let uz = az + bz * t;

    let wt = omega * t;
    let c = wt.cos();
    let s = wt.sin();

    // ζ = u · (cos ωt − i·sin ωt)
    let y = uy * c + uz * s;
    let z = uz * c - uy * s;

    // ζ̇ = (B − iω·u) · e^(−iωt)
    let wy = by + omega * uz;
    let wz = bz - omega * uy;
    let vy = wy * c + wz * s;
    let vz = wz * c - wy * s;

    PointState {
        p: Vec3::new(x, y, z),
        v: Vec3::new(vx, vy, vz),
    }
}

In game/rig-core/src/analysis.rs, Ember exploits a crucial algebraic property of this closed form: since $|e^{-i\omega t}| = 1$, the radial distance from the cylinder spine at any time $t$ is simply the modulus of a linear function of time:

$$|\zeta(t)| = |\zeta_0 + v_{\text{rot}} t| = \sqrt{(y_0 + (v_{y0} - \omega z_0)t)^2 + (z_0 + (v_{z0} + \omega y_0)t)^2}$$

Consequently, a throw avoids striking the outer cylinder skin ($|\zeta(t)| < R$) over a long flight time $t_{\text{flight}}$ if and only if the rotating-frame velocity $v_{\text{rot}} = (v_{y0} - \omega z_0) + i(v_{z0} + \omega y_0)$ nearly vanishes—that is, when the player's cross-plane throw velocity almost cancels the centrifugal sweep $\omega \zeta_0$. Meanwhile, the $e^{-i\omega t}$ factor winds the velocity heading at rate $\omega\,\text{rad/s}$. This mathematical insight enabled analysis.rs's deterministic coarse-to-fine solver to discover a human-missed scoring Loop from $x = -180\,\text{m}$ to the gate at $x = +320\,\text{m}$ ($500\,\text{m}$ downfield, $v_x \approx 18\,\text{m/s}$, $v_\perp \approx 0.4\,\text{m/s}$, $t_{\text{flight}} \approx 28\,\text{s}$, accumulating $\gtrsim 9\,\text{rad} \gg \text{LOOP\_TURN} = 2.2\,\text{rad}$ without touching the $R = 45\,\text{m}$ skin). Furthermore, in commit fd6ce91 (2026-05-20, "Use analytical Coriolis predictor for receiver in lead solver"), Ember replaced linear extrapolation of moving receivers in game/rig-core/src/ai/lead_predict.rs with trajectory::analytic, allowing AI passers to lead airborne receivers along their true curved Coriolis trajectories.

1.3 Constrained Optimization ("The Number") & 6-DOF Gyroscopic Bell

Rather than hand-tuning habitat dimensions and spin rates (which had previously oscillated across $\omega \in \{0.22, 0.06, 0.15, 0.32\}$), Ember formulated the game's physical constants in game/rig-core/src/tuning.rs as a constrained optimization gate ("The Number") enforced by cargo test:

ConstantValuePhysical / Gameplay Role
OMEGA ($\omega$)0.32 rad/sReference cylinder spin rate (barrel-roll period $2\pi/\omega \approx 19.63\,\text{s}$)
R45.0 mPlayable calm cylinder skin radius ($g(R) = \omega^2 R = 4.608\,\text{m/s}^2 \approx 0.47\,g_\oplus$)
L640.0 mAxial field length ($x \in [-320, +320]\,\text{m}$)
GATE_RADIUS8.0 mScoring ring radius at GATE_X = ±320.0 m
LINE_K / LINE_C1400.0 / 520.0Taut rig-line radial spring stiffness & damping ($\omega_n \approx 4.24\,\text{rad/s}, \zeta \approx 0.55$)
REEL_PULL_SPEED / ACCEL26.0 m/s / 120.0 m/s²Active Xonotic-style winch cruise speed and acceleration cap
CLAW_SPEED80.0 m/sFinite grapple claw travel speed (ceil(distance * 3) ticks at 240 Hz)
FRICTION_DECAY0.9753099120283326Frozen bit-identical literal for $\exp(-6.0 / 240.0)$ tangential skin friction

The ball itself is simulated as a full 6-DOF rigid body (BellBody) with an internal symmetric-top mass ring in game/rig-core/src/bell.rs. Its principal moments of inertia in the body frame (where the ring axis is $+\hat{x}$) are $I = \text{diag}(I_{\text{AXIAL}}, I_{\text{TRANS}}, I_{\text{TRANS}}) = \text{diag}(1.0, 0.5, 0.5)$. At every $h = 1/240\,\text{s}$ tick, step_bell integrates $(p, v, q, w)$ via 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) over torque-free Euler's equations:

$$I \dot{\vec{\omega}}_{\text{body}} = -\vec{\omega}_{\text{body}} \times (I \vec{\omega}_{\text{body}}), \qquad \dot{q} = \frac{1}{2} \vec{\omega}_{\text{world}} \otimes q$$

When a thrower imparts pure axial spin ($\vec{\omega}_{\text{body}} \parallel \hat{x}$), $\vec{\omega} \times (I\vec{\omega}) = 0$, so trueness(w) = |w.x| / |w| = 1.0 and chime(w) voices the pure harmonic bell oscillators in game/src/audio/AudioEngine.ts. When a defender knocks the bell off-axis, gyroscopic precession tumbles the body, dropping trueness(w) and cross-fading WebAudio to detuned inharmonic metallic partials (inharmonicOsc, flutterLfo)—a literal clatter.

1.4 Powered Grapple Winch, Claw Latency, Spar Anchoring & Thrumbler Micro-Control

In game/rig-core/src/grapple.rs, resolve_line models the rigger's tether across three physical regimes:

  1. Powered Winch (reel < 0 on fixed anchor): Because the calm near the axis is weightless ($\omega^2 r \approx 0.8\,\text{m/s}^2$), a passive pendulum rope cannot propel a stationary rigger. Reeling in shrinks line.rest_len at REEL_RATE and applies an acceleration-capped motor impulse (dv = deficit.min(REEL_PULL_ACCEL * h)) up to REEL_PULL_SPEED = 26.0 m/s.
  2. Slack Pre-Tension Band (stretch > -LINE_SLACK_BAND) & Taut Spring (stretch >= 0): Prevents discontinuous velocity snaps by easing into tautness with LINE_SLACK_K = 120.0 before engaging the main radial spring-damper $F_{\text{pull}} = \max(0, k_{\text{eff}} \cdot \text{stretch} + c_{\text{eff}} \cdot v_{\text{rad}})$.
  3. Momentum-Conserving Player-to-Player Tethers: When line.anchor_player is Some(teammate_or_opponent), resolve_line computes the reduced inverse mass $w_{\text{sum}} = m_p^{-1} + m_a^{-1}$ and applies equal-and-opposite impulses $\Delta \vec{v}_p = -j m_p^{-1} \hat{n}$ and $\Delta \vec{v}_a = +j m_a^{-1} \hat{n}$, verified by unit tests player_player_conserves_momentum and player_player_conserves_momentum_moving_anchor to conserve linear momentum to $< 10^{-6}$.

Three critical locomotion refinements landed on 2026-05-20:

  • Fix Stuck-on-Spar (38e3ba6): Players winching into a structural spar previously remained tethered after reaching the anchor or after the spar fell behind their target vector. Commit 38e3ba6 added an arrival/alignment check in rigger_ai.rs that releases the line when within $4\,\text{m}$ of the spar or when $\hat{d}_{\text{anchor}} \cdot \hat{d}_{\text{target}} < 0.1$.
  • Downrange Anchor & Longer Rollout (358f3a0): Extended the grapple planner (game/rig-core/src/planner.rs) rollout horizon and weighted downrange velocity alignment so riggers sling past spars rather than stopping at them.
  • Thrumbler Coriolis Drift Counteraction (e09cbfb, a78a7e6, 2ad529c): In game/rig-core/src/ai/rigger_ai.rs, settle_thrumbler governs the rigger's cold-gas micro-thrusters (MICRO_DV_MAX = 3.5 m/s). Inside SETTLE_RADIUS = 18.0 m, it performs proportional-derivative braking onto the station-keeping target; outside 18.0 m (commit 2ad529c), if the rigger is already closing ($v_{\text{toward}} > 3.0\,\text{m/s}$), it spends $15\%$ of MICRO_DV_MAX purely to brake perpendicular Coriolis drift ($v_\perp > 4.0\,\text{m/s}$), and otherwise applies a gentle $20\%$ forward push.

1.5 Active Inference (EFE) Pack Behavior & Learned WASM Locomotion (rl::loco)

The tactical AI in game/rig-core/src/ai/ combines an Expected Free Energy (efe.rs, efe_params.rs) spatial coverage evaluator with role-specific state machines (roles/{anchor,spinner,faithwing,freewing,reach}.rs) and a Director (director.rs). In commit 74e0001 (2026-05-20, "PACK BEHAVIOR: collapse positioning to cluster around the ball"), Ember diagnosed why early matches looked like "seven spectators orbiting at 70–90m while one player did something": the EFE anti-swarm term was pushing off-ball players across a $160\,\text{m}$ axial spread. Commit 74e0001 collapsed candidate fan depths from [-70, +10, +90] to [-15, +10, +35], reduced cross-tube radii from 14–40 m to 10–28 m, cut anti-swarm standoff from 18 m / weight 2.5 to 8 m / weight 0.5, and capped receiver leads at 30–60 m, producing cohesive pack flow around the bell.

Finally, in commits 7f6ac77 and bcb3ed4 (2026-05-20), Ember added a learned neural locomotion policy in game/rig-core/src/rl/loco.rs and an Evolution Strategies (ES) trainer in game/rig-core/src/rl/loco_train.rs (train_loco binary):

  • Architecture: A pure-f64, zero-allocation, WASM-safe 2-hidden-layer MLP with LOCO_FEAT_W = 40 input features (normalized self position/velocity, target relative vector/distance, velocity decomposition into radial/tangential components, Coriolis acceleration vector, current line state, and relative coordinates of the K_SPAR = 3 nearest structural spars), hidden width HID = 48 ($\tanh$ activations), and LOCO_OUT_W = 13 control outputs (aim, fire_line_at, reel, release, pushoff, thrumbler), totaling exactly LOCO_PARAM_W = 4,957 parameters.
  • Team-Level RL (rl/mappo.rs & rig-gym-py): Alongside rl::loco, game/rig-core/src/rl/ implements Multi-Agent PPO (mappo.rs) with entity self-attention (attention.rs), centralized value networks (value.rs), and a PyO3/Gymnasium vectorized bridge (game/rig-gym-py).

2. don, automatafl & webapp2-auto — Binary-Oracle RTS Reconstruction, Deterministic GPU Flow Fields & Zero-Twin Lean 4 Game Kernels

2.1 don (Descent of Nations): Architecture & The DataWalk 15-Channel Fidelity Oracle

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/don (git@github.com:emberian/don.git, 1,003 commits on HEAD through f219bd03 on 2026-10-04, 1,129 total commits across refs).

Descent of Nations is an independent, deterministic Rust reconstruction of Big Huge Games' 2003 RTS Rise of Nations: Thrones and Patriots, engineered simultaneously as a standalone moddable game, a binary-verified fidelity reference, and a high-throughput reinforcement learning environment (README.md). Its 21-crate workspace (Cargo.toml) is partitioned into:

  • State, Serialization & Lockstep Checksums (crates/don-state): Built on the retail engine's own DataWalk visitor pattern (crates/don-state/src/lib.rs). Rather than inventing ad-hoc Rust structs and guessing serialization formats, don-state transcribes each C++ class's walk_data method once (crates/don-state/src/sections.rs, crates/don-state/src/walk.rs). Driving the visitor with Loader parses .svx retail save games while recording byte-exact Span attributions; driving it with Saver re-emits byte-identical .svx streams; driving it with CheckSum computes all 15 retail lockstep Adler-32 checksum channels (CHANNEL_NAMES in crates/don-state/src/check_all.rs, completed in commits b2b7aaf0 and 4274eaa0 on 2026-10-04).
  • Retail-Ordered Frame Schedule (crates/don-state/src/tick.rs & crates/don-sim): In crates/don-state/src/tick.rs, STEPS codifies the exact 29-step execution sequence of retail's Game::do_frame (0x005926b0), mapping each step to its exact x86 virtual address (va) and implementation status (Ported vs Stub), including Objects::inc_time, Game::process_commands, PathFinder::process, Objects::process, Armies::process, City::process, Build::process, Territory::process, Leaders::process, Research::process, and Leaders::end_process.

2.2 In-Process i686 Binary Differential Oracle & Live Retail Control

To prevent the Rust port from drifting from the shipped x86 machine code, crates/oracle/src/lib.rs and crates/oracle/src/image.rs map the actual retail riseofnations.exe binary into a live 32-bit x86 process (i686), apply base relocations, construct fabricated C++ thiscall / fastcall world memory (damage_env.rs), and run fork-isolated differential fuzz/mutation trials directly against the Rust functions in don-sim. As recorded in README.md and schema/oracle-regression.json, the oracle has executed 18,722,565 trials across 23 registered x86 function cases with zero mismatches, skips, or crashes.

Complementing offline differential testing, tools/retail-control/retail_control.c (485c9ef4) and tools/rontoy-host/ (crates/rontoy-core, crates/rontoy-proto) inject a hash-bound DLL into a live running retail process, enabling read-only state capture, paused-frame .svx + 15-channel check_all extraction, live economy coaching, and reversible main-thread command ingress that restores stock instruction bytes cleanly on detach.

2.3 don-gpu: Temporally-Blocked WGSL Integer Flow-Field Relaxation & Abelian ECS Reductions

In crates/don-gpu/src/lib.rs, Ember solves the classic RTS GPU determinism problem: how do you run batched pathfinding and branchy unit-order execution across thousands of parallel RL environments on a GPU without floating-point drift or atomic scheduling non-determinism?

The solution has two halves:

  1. Min-Plus Tropical Flow Fields in WGSL (crates/don-gpu/src/shaders/flowfield.wgsl): Every distance and terrain cost is a u32 (W_CARD = 2u, W_DIAG = 3u, INF = 0x7fffffffu, BLOCKED = 0xffffffffu). Because integer + is exact and $\min$ is associative, commutative, and idempotent, the Jacobi fixed point is strictly independent of GPU warp/workgroup scheduling. Each workgroup of $8 \times 8 = 64$ threads loads an $8 \times 8$ tile plus a 1-cell halo ($10 \times 10 = 100$ u32 cells in var<workgroup> sd: array<u32, 100>) and runs params.inner_steps Jacobi relaxations in shared memory before writing back to global memory. A per-field atomic flag (flags: array<atomic<u32>>) and an active_list buffer allow the host (crates/don-gpu/src/gpu.rs) to stream-compact converged worlds out of subsequent dispatches, avoiding up to $23\times$ wasted GPU work.
wgsl
// /Users/ember/dev/don/crates/don-gpu/src/shaders/flowfield.wgsl (lines 89-118)
    // ---- temporally blocked Jacobi -----------------------------------------------------
    // `params.inner_steps` is uniform across the whole dispatch, so both barriers sit in
    // uniform control flow, as WGSL requires.
    for (var s: u32 = 0u; s < params.inner_steps; s = s + 1u) {
        let card = min(min(sd[idx - HALO], sd[idx - 1u]), min(sd[idx + 1u], sd[idx + HALO]));
        let diag = min(min(sd[idx - HALO - 1u], sd[idx - HALO + 1u]),
                       min(sd[idx + HALO - 1u], sd[idx + HALO + 1u]));
        let best = min(sd[idx], min(card + c2, diag + c3));
        workgroupBarrier();
        sd[idx] = best;
        workgroupBarrier();
    }

    if (inside) {
        let final_d = sd[idx];
        dst[gi] = final_d;
        if (final_d != original) {
            atomicStore(&wg_changed, 1u);
        }
    }
    workgroupBarrier();
    if (li == 0u && atomicLoad(&wg_changed) != 0u) {
        atomicStore(&flags[field], 1u);
    }
  1. Order-Archetype Bucketing & Atomic-Free Abelian Reductions (crates/don-gpu/src/partition.rs, crates/don-gpu/src/reduce.rs): As Ember writes in don-gpu/src/lib.rs: "branchiness is a property of the layout, not of the problem." By radix-sorting entities by their 28 retail Order archetypes (ORDER_NAMES measured from schema/symbols.json) via Partition, per-entity virtual dispatch turns into 28 homogeneous branch-free kernels. Many-to-one state writes (e.g., multiple gatherers depositing resources or multiple attackers damaging one target) never use GPU atomics; instead, accumulate_i32 performs a segmented reduction over sorted target keys in the abelian group $(\mathbb{Z}/2^{32}\mathbb{Z}, \text{wrapping\_add})$, while draw_from_pools uses a segmented exclusive scan to reproduce sequential resource depletion bit-for-bit.

2.4 don-bhs & don-env: Reconstructed BHS Stack VM & Dual-Surface RL Environments

In crates/don-bhs/src/lib.rs, Ember reverse-engineered Big Huge Games' proprietary .bhs / .bhc scripting language, shipping a full source compiler (crates/don-bhs-cc), bytecode disassembler (disasm.rs), stack VM (vm.rs supporting frame-persistent static variables guarded by OP_JUMP_IF_INITED = 0x44), and a table of all retail builtins (builtin_table.rs, BUILTINS). In crates/don-env/src/lib.rs, don-env exposes the simulation to RL agents via two explicitly separated backends (EnvironmentBackend):

  • VecEnv: High-throughput, vectorized compact environment refactoring the 82 retail CommandTypes opcodes and 28 OrderIndex kinds into 10 independently masked action heads (FactoredUnitActionSpace), with zero-copy observations derived from schema/state-schema.json and 11-term LeaderData score rewards.
  • AuthoritativeBackend: Fail-closed single-episode fidelity backend backed by don_sim::tick::Sim, returning typed refusal proofs (ApplyRefusal, AttackTargetEligibilityRefusal, VisibilityCaptureRefusal) rather than silently accepting unimplemented actions as no-ops.

2.5 automatafl & webapp2-auto: Zero-Twin Lean 4 Kernel, Tarjan SCC Resolution & Simultaneous-Move Game Theory

Repositories: /Users/ember/dev/automatafl (63 commits on HEAD through 97db66a on 2026-11-02, 69 commits across refs) and /Users/ember/dev/webapp2-auto.

automatafl is a simultaneous-move tactical abstract board game on an $N \times N$ grid ($7 \times 7$ blitz7, $9 \times 9$ tactical9, or $11 \times 11$ classic11) where two or more players secretly commit rook-slides of shared Repulsors (R, code 1) and Attractors (A, code 2) through vacuum (0) to herd an autonomous cellular Automaton (@, code 3) into their corner goals (README.md).

The Zero-Twin Lean 4 Architecture & Verbatim Theorems

To eliminate any possibility of divergence between the formal specification, the Axum multiplayer server (automatafl-server), the terminal client (automatafl-client), and the browser WASM bundle, Ember deleted the standalone Rust rule engine and established a Zero-Twin Lean 4 core under lean/Automatafl/:

  • Lean 4 compiles Base.lean, Rules.lean, Termination.lean, Variants.lean, PackedBoard.lean, and FFI.lean to C IR (lean/.lake/build/ir/Automatafl/*.c), which automatafl-lean/build.rs compiles and links against a stripped C runtime shim (automatafl-lean/c/lean_shim.c).
  • In lean/Automatafl/Base.lean and lean/Automatafl/Rules.lean, Ember proves decidability of move legality, totality and Manhattan-bound safety of the Automaton's axial sightline step, particle conservation (resolve_conserves), and full permutation invariance (Principle of Fairness) of simultaneous move resolution:
lean
-- /Users/ember/dev/automatafl/lean/Automatafl/Rules.lean (lines 145-158, 422-429, 1034-1036, 1207-1232)
/-- Move legality against a board and the round's conflict markers. -/
def MoveLegal (b : Board) (marks : List Coord) (m : Move) : Prop :=
  m.frm ≠ m.to
  ∧ (m.frm.x = m.to.x ∨ m.frm.y = m.to.y)
  ∧ b.inBounds m.frm ∧ b.inBounds m.to
  ∧ ¬ b.isAutomaton m.frm
  ∧ m.frm ∉ marks ∧ m.to ∉ marks

theorem moveLegalB_iff (b : Board) (marks : List Coord) (m : Move) :
    moveLegalB b marks m = true ↔ MoveLegal b marks m := by
  unfold moveLegalB; exact decide_eq_true_iff

/-- The automaton moves AT MOST one step in a cardinal direction, for every tie-break. -/
theorem automatonOffsetCfg_bounded (b : Board) (tb : TieBreak) :
    (automatonOffsetCfg b tb).1.natAbs + (automatonOffsetCfg b tb).2.natAbs ≤ 1 := by ...

theorem resolve_conserves (b : Board) (ms : List Move) :
    Conserves b (resolveMoves b ms) (conservePhi b ms) := by ...

/-- The move graph is permutation-invariant. -/
theorem edgeMap_perm {ms₁ ms₂ : List Move} (h : ms₁.Perm ms₂) (b : Board) :
    edgeMap b ms₁ = edgeMap b ms₂ := by ...

theorem landMap_perm {ms₁ ms₂ : List Move} (h : ms₁.Perm ms₂) (b : Board) :
    landMap b ms₁ = landMap b ms₂ := by
  unfold landMap
  rw [edgeMap_perm h b, h.length_eq]
  • Well-Founded Clash-Round Termination (lean/Automatafl/Termination.lean): When two players' moves conflict in default Conflict mode, the contested squares are added to rs.marks, colliding moves are unlocked, and the round re-opens (.again rs'). Ember proved in Termination.lean that under the RoundWF invariant (marksNodup, marksInBounds, lockedLegal), every .again transition strictly increases rs.marks.length (roundStep_marks_strict_growth) while remaining bounded by $N^2$, discharging termination of multi-attempt simultaneous rounds.
  • 2-Bit-Per-Cell PackedBoard & Bitmask128 Equivalence (lean/Automatafl/PackedBoard.lean): For zero-allocation AI search across UInt64 bitboards (Bitmask128), PackedBoard.lean proves bit-level lens laws (testBit_setBit_self, testBit_setBit_ne, testBit_clearBit_self, PackedBoard.unpack_pack_cellAt_eq) and #assert_all_clean conformance across all confluence modes (.conflict, .bunchBefore, .annihilate) and twoCycleSwaps.
  • Simultaneous-Move Game-Theoretic Bots (automatafl-ai/src/lib.rs): Because Automatafl is a simultaneous-move game where standard sequential alpha-beta is unsound, automatafl-ai implements four specialized engines over PackedRoundState:
  • BotKind::Greedy (GreedyHeuristicBot): 1-ply sightline and goal-distance evaluator (eval.rs).
  • BotKind::Minimax (SimultaneousMinimaxBot in minimax.rs): Maximin / alpha-beta matrix game solver.
  • BotKind::DecoupledUct (DecoupledUctBot in duct.rs): Decoupled UCT (DUCB) simultaneous-move Monte Carlo Tree Search.
  • BotKind::RegretMatching (RegretMatchingBot in regret.rs): Regret Matching Plus (RM+) mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium solver.

3.1 bw-exp0, bw-exp1, and blackwing-v0: The Blackwing Multi-Genre Engine & Holdsmith Z3 Verifier

3.2 frisqueendom & friskingdom: 6-DOF Aerodynamic Disc Physics & Bevy Ultimate Frisbee

Repositories: /Users/ember/dev/frisqueendom (27 commits through 0b373a5 on 2026-02-17) and /Users/ember/dev/friskingdom (2 commits through 8cc2477 on 2026-02-09, 29 commits combined).

Both repositories share a first-principles 6-DOF rigid-body aerodynamic disc simulator (frisqueendom/frisque-physics/src/aero.rs and frisqueendom/frisque-physics/src/disc.rs, ported into Bevy in friskingdom/crates/frisbee-physics). The standard 175g Ultrastar disc is parameterized by default_ultimate_disc():

  • Mass $m = 0.175\,\text{kg}$, diameter $d = 0.273\,\text{m}$, planform area $A = \pi (d/2)^2 \approx 0.0585\,\text{m}^2$, axial moment of inertia $I_{\text{axial}} = 0.00235\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$, pitch/roll moment of inertia $I_{\text{pitch}} = 0.00122\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$.
  • Given relative air velocity $\vec{v}_{\text{rel}} = \vec{v}_{\text{disc}} - \vec{v}_{\text{wind}}$ (where wind includes Perlin/simplex turbulence in wind.rs and noise.rs) and air density $\rho = 1.225\,\text{kg/m}^3$, aero.rs computes:
  • Angle of Attack ($\alpha$): Rotates $\vec{v}_{\text{rel}}$ into the disc body frame via $q^* \vec{v}_{\text{rel}} q$ and computes $\alpha = \text{atan2}(-v_{\text{body},y}, \sqrt{v_{\text{body},x}^2 + v_{\text{body},z}^2})$.
  • Lift with Smoothstep Stall Falloff (compute_lift): Linear lift $C_L(\alpha) = \min(C_{L,\max}, C_{L0} + C_{L\alpha} \alpha)$ ($C_{L0} = 0.15, C_{L\alpha} = 1.4, C_{L,\max} = 1.1$) up to stall onset $0.8 \alpha_{\text{stall}}$ ($\alpha_{\text{stall}} = 0.785\,\text{rad} \approx 45^\circ$), followed by a $C^1$-continuous cubic Hermite (smoothstep = t*t*(3.0 - 2.0*t)) $60\%$ lift collapse, amplified near the turf ($y \le 2d$) by compute_ground_effect: $$F_{\text{lift}} = \frac{1}{2} \rho v_{\text{air}}^2 A C_L(\alpha) \cdot \left(1 + 0.5 \max\left(0, 1 - \frac{y}{2d}\right)\right)$$
  • Quadratic Induced Drag (compute_drag): $C_D(\alpha) = C_{D0} + C_{D\alpha} \alpha^2$ ($0.08 + 2.2\alpha^2$).
  • Gyroscopic Pitching Moment & Spin Decay (compute_pitching_moment, compute_spin_down): Pitching moment $M = \frac{1}{2}\rho v_{\text{air}}^2 A d (C_{m0} + C_{m\alpha} \alpha_{\text{deg}})$ along state.disc_right(). Because the disc has high axial spin $\omega_y$, this pitching torque around the lateral axis induces gyroscopic roll precession (making a RHBH throw bank left as it slows down).

In friskingdom, this physics core drives an 11-crate Bevy 0.18 workspace (friskingdom/Cargo.toml) featuring procedural stickman animation (design-docs/05-stickman-animation.md), stack/cutting offensive and marking defensive AI (crates/fk-ai/src/{offense,defense,throwing}.rs), deterministic rollback/snapshot netcode (crates/fk-netcode), season management (crates/fk-season), and a Python MCP server (tools/mcp-game-server/server.py) that lets an AI agent inspect and drive live Bevy ECS game states.

Identity Linking (NameId & same_name_groups): engine.chronoport(entity_id, target_tick) validates window_past / window_future constraints (0x140008 / 0x140010), marks the source entity LifecycleState::Chronoporting, and spawns a LifecycleState::Prebirth duplicate at target_tick sharing the same NameId so paradox-resolution rules (such as the Grandfather Paradox in examples/paradox.rs) can iterate over get_same_name_entities(id).

4.1 audec, audec-wt & audec-ui-platform-probe: The Reverse DAW, AIR Deprojection & Incremental Preroll Bounce

Repositories:

  • /Users/ember/dev/audec (436 commits on HEAD through 745adec on 2026-09-13, ~484 across campaign worktrees)
  • /Users/ember/dev/audec-wt (39 vertical-slice commit records *-commit*.txt + bounce/ workspace snapshot)
  • /Users/ember/dev/audec-ui-platform-probe (4 commits through dcba607 on 2026-09-01)

Doctrine: Decompiling Audio into an Auditory Intermediate Representation (AIR)

As defined in audec/README.md and audec/docs/VISION.md, audec is a native multiwindow Rust + GPUI reverse DAW: "A DAW begins with tracks, notes, automation, effects, and routing, then renders them into audio. audec starts with the audio and works in the other direction: recording → measurements → events and gestures → patterns and sources → editable hypotheses → reconstruction + unexplained residual."

Just as a binary decompiler lifts machine code into an intermediate representation with address provenance without claiming to recover lost source comments, audec lifts recorded sound into an Auditory Intermediate Representation (AIR) whose objects retain exact links to the sample spans and content-addressed DSP transforms that proposed them:

  • Five Synchronized Analysis Lenses (src/ui/lens_*.rs):
  • Waterfall (src/ui/lens_waterfall.rs & src/cqt.rs): Retained numeric dB field supporting live switching between FFT and a deterministic multiresolution Constant-Q Transform (ConstantQ) at 24 bins per octave (minimum_frequency_hz: 27.5, maximum_frequency_hz: 8_000.0, hop_size: 256, CqtWindow::{Hann, Blackman, BlackmanHarris, Rectangular}). Bins with similar window lengths share an FFT plan while frequency-domain kernels are sparsified at SPARSE_RELATIVE_AMPLITUDE = 1.0e-5.
  • Rhythm Deprojection (src/ui/lens_rhythm.rs & src/beat_this_deprojection.rs): Multiband spectral novelty analysis, ranked integer tempo hypotheses, beat/downbeat evidence (workers/beat_this_worker.py / src/bin/audec-beat-this-worker.rs), and anonymous hit-family clustering with auditionable medoids (4807fad, 4c9986c).
  • Components (src/ui/lens_components.rs): Deterministic convolutional NMF extracting 8-frame frequency-by-lag gesture templates and activation histories (72608b1, 364e7df).
  • Decomposition (src/ui/lens_hpss.rs): Selection-local Harmonic-Percussive Source Separation (HPSS) with configurable kernel knobs (369ca7c, 87b16c4) and audible residual/mixture nulling.
  • Loom (src/ui/lens_loom.rs): Phase-preserving attack alignment deprojected into an editable event sequence (docs/design/LOOM_LIVE_EDITS.md).

Shareable Content-Addressed Readings & Atomic Deprojection DAG Execution

In src/reading.rs and docs/READINGS.md, analytical interpretations are packaged as portable audec-reading v1 documents (ReadingId([u8; 16])). A reading never embeds copyrighted source PCM and never claims global authority: every entity is namespace-qualified by QualifiedEntityId { reading: ReadingId, kind: String, local_id: u64 }, allowing multiple competing human or agent readings of the same recording to be imported, merged, and verified side-by-side (src/comparison_runtime.rs).

Meanwhile, src/deprojection_execution.rs enforces atomic generation discipline over asynchronous native analyzers and isolated out-of-process workers (src/worker_broker.rs, src/bin/audec-clap-worker.rs): DeprojectionExecution tracks each DAG node via NodeLease { run: DeprojectionRunToken, node: DeprojectionNodeId } and refuses to attach late worker completions to a superseded project generation.

Incremental Bounce-on-Play (TileKey, ConsumedRevisionStamp & TailPolicy)

Rather than maintaining a separate real-time lock-free DSP graph that can diverge from offline export, audec enforces a single-engine doctrine in docs/RENDER_TILES.md, src/render_tiles.rs, and src/daw_engine.rs: playback is an incremental tiled bounce of the offline renderer, so online/offline nulling holds by construction.

rust
// /Users/ember/dev/audec/src/render_tiles.rs (lines 48-95)
pub const DEFAULT_TILE_CONTEXT_FRAMES: u64 = 4 * DEFAULT_TILE_FRAMES as u64;

/// Revisions the v1 master product actually consumes. AIR remains outside the
/// forward audio graph, so an evidence-only edit can re-key every tile without
/// rerendering PCM.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, Hash, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct ConsumedRevisionStamp {
    pub arrangement: u64,
    pub sequencer: u64,
    pub automation: u64,
    pub assets: u64,
    pub mixer: u64,
    pub sample_kits: u64,
    pub bindings: u64,
}
  • Each timeline tile of length DEFAULT_TILE_FRAMES ($2^{16} = 65,536$ frames $\approx 1.49\,\text{s}$ at $44.1\,\text{kHz}$) is content-addressed by TileKey { scope, tile_index, tile_frames, inputs } where inputs binds the ConsumedRevisionStamp and engine configuration hash.
  • Because ConsumedRevisionStamp excludes AIR analysis domains, editing analytical hypotheses re-keys tiles in $O(1)$ without re-rendering audio.
  • To prevent sampler voices or clip fades triggered in tile $i - 1$ from being truncated at the boundary of tile $i$, every tile render computes a schedule-derived TailPolicy { preroll_frames } (bounded by DEFAULT_TILE_CONTEXT_FRAMES), renders the preroll window prior to tile_index * tile_frames, and discards the preroll samples before caching the tile.

Three technical subsystems make vidbox extraordinary:

  1. Musical Signal Compiler (render/signals.py & render/comp.py):
  2. Every visual parameter (layer opacity, scale, position along timed cubic Bézier trajectories render/bezier.py, audio gain, or shader effect intensity in render/fx.py and render/fx_extra.py) can be bound to a declarative musical signal evaluated against projects/meine/analysis/beats.json (Music): beat-phase envelopes (decay, pulse, saw, ramp, sine, tri), exponential onset followers (onset_env(t, tau=0.15, minimum=0.3)), smoothed song-intensity curves, and impact-aligned clip placement (c.footage(s, at=c.bar(20), hit=h) so the exact explosion frame lands on the downbeat).
  3. Interval-Union Revisited-Span Decoder (render/tl.py):
  4. When a timeline layer stutters, loops on the beat grid, or plays in reverse via a TimeMap, re-seeking FFmpeg per frame would destroy throughput. revisit_spans(tm, t0, t1) scans all runs in the TimeMap over [t0, t1) using sorted disjoint interval unions (_union_add with bisect_left/bisect_right) to identify source intervals traversed backward (np.any(np.diff(s) < -1e-9)) or visited more than once, pre-decoding only those unioned spans into memory in $O(n)$ rather than $O(n^2)$ overlap pieces.
  5. Executable Ethical & Documentary Design Rule Checker (render/drc.py):
  6. projects/meine/comps/full.py refuses to build the timeline if render/drc.py reports any ERROR across rules that directly codify Ember's documentary ethics and aesthetic judgments:

# /Users/ember/dev/vidbox/render/drc.py (lines 110-189)
@rule("scope", "ERROR", 'ember: "the problem isn\'t the strike into people, the problem is that it isn\'t Israel/Gaza at all."')
def r_scope(P):
    allowed = set(IN_SCOPE) | set(P.tl.get("scope_allow", []))
    return [(L["t0"], f"{L['id']}: scope {P.scope(L)}") for L in P.L
            if P.footage(L) and P.scope(L) not in allowed and P.scope(L) is not None]

@rule("voronoi-faces-only", "ERROR", 'ember: "do *not* use the voronoi effect on war footage, but it looks AMAZING on the guys face."')
def r_voronoi(P):
    out = [(L["t0"], f"{L['id']}: {f['op']} on footage") for L in P.L if P.footage(L)
           for f in L.get("fx", []) if f.get("op") in HEADS_ONLY_FX]
    out += [(0.0, f"post: {f['op']} over the whole frame") for f in P.tl.get("post", []) if f.get("op") in HEADS_ONLY_FX]
    return out

@rule("no-decoration-on-the-dead", "ERROR", 'ember: "no decoration on the dead, no mocking juxtaposition, full truth."')
def r_decoration(P):
    out = []
    for L in P.L:
        clip, seg = P.seg(L)
        if seg and seg.get("graphic", 0) >= 2 and (L.get("fx") or L.get("blend", "normal") != "normal"):
            ops = ",".join(f["op"] for f in L.get("fx", [])) or L.get("blend")
            out.append((L["t0"], f"{L['id']}: graphic {seg['graphic']} footage under {ops}"))
    return out

scrubsheet: Browser-Native Video Contact Sheet Editor

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/scrubsheet (3 commits on 2026-09-17 through bedb00f).

In scrubsheet/README.md, app.js, media.js, and drafts.js, Ember built a zero-dependency vanilla JS video contact-sheet studio featuring:

  • Dual-Decoder Non-Destructive Filmstrip (media.js): Generates 8-thumbnail timeline filmstrips with up to 32× zoom around the playhead and Seed empty cells batch sampling using an offscreen secondary video element so thumbnail extraction never perturbs or seeks the user's primary playback decoder.
  • 144-Candidate Frame Tray & 30-Step Undo (app.js): Supports continuous rolling capture (keep rolling after capture), cell drag-swapping, letterbox vs. crop aspect-ratio matching, and .scrubsheet JSON serialization.
  • Per-Tab IndexedDB Draft Recovery (drafts.js): Persists captured frames, tray candidates, and playhead timestamps in IndexedDB with tab-session isolation.

4.4 codrawer-bridge: Raw evdev reMarkable Paper Pro Daemon, 50-RPM AI Ghost Ink & iPad Rocq IDE

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/codrawer-bridge (8 commits from 2025-12-11 to 1127f5d on 2026-02-09).

codrawer-bridge connects physical e-paper and tablet styluses to a real-time collaborative AI drawing and formal proof workspace across three components:

  1. reMarkable Paper Pro Raw Input Daemon (bridge/remarkable/codrawer_bridge.py):
  2. Runs directly on the reMarkable Paper Pro without requiring python-evdev: it parses /proc/bus/input/devices to score and select the Wacom/stylus /dev/input/event* node, reads raw kernel input_event structs (EV_KEY = 0x01, EV_ABS = 0x03, BTN_TOUCH = 0x14A, ABS_X = 0x00, ABS_Y = 0x01, ABS_PRESSURE = 0x18), normalizes $(x, y, p) \in [0, 1]^3$ against hardware EVIOCGABS ranges (AbsRanges), and streams stroke_begin, 60 Hz batched stroke_pts (MAX_BATCH_POINTS = 64), and stroke_end frames over WebSocket while leaving CODRAWER_GRAB = 0 by default so native e-ink rendering stays <16ms (docs/latency_budget.md).
  3. Stroke-Native Router & Rate-Limited Ghost Ink (docs/protocol.md, src/codrawer_bridge/server/, model-server/):
  4. Enforces a strict two-layer separation: layer="user" is immutable human ink; layer="ai" is streamed ghost ink (ai_stroke_begin, ai_stroke_pts, ai_stroke_end) triggered exclusively on stroke_end (or explicit prompt messages in "draw" / "handwriting" modes) with debouncing (DEBOUNCE_S) and a hard MIN_MODEL_INTERVAL_S governor respecting a 50 RPM ($\approx 0.83\,\text{req/s}$) model ceiling.
  5. Native iPad Client with PencilKit & Rocq Prover IDE (codrawer-ipad/Codrawer/Sources/):
  6. Added in commits 8d22800, d502feb, and 3160089 (2026-02-09): a native SwiftUI iPad app combining a low-latency Apple PencilKit canvas (Views/CanvasView.swift) that renders streamed AI ghost strokes in real time alongside an integrated Rocq (Coq) Prover IDE (Views/RocqEditor.swift) with split-screen .v proof script editing and live proof-goal inspection.

5. Multiphysics & Nuclear Reactor Simulation (plymouth-rock & buckeye)

5.1 plymouth-rock: 350 MWt Natrium-Style Sodium Fast Reactor Simulator (Rust gdext + Godot 4 + Blender MCP)

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/plymouth-rock.

plymouth-rock is an integrated multiphysics simulator for a 350 MWt / 140 MWe Natrium-class Sodium-Cooled Fast Reactor (SFR) coupled to a 2 GWh two-tank molten salt thermal storage system (README.md). Its Rust physics core (rust/src/lib.rs) compiles as a gdext dynamic library (libplymouth_rock_core.dylib) driving a 3D Godot 4 control room (godot/src/control_room.gd) whose 3D core geometry (godot/assets/reactor_core.glb) was procedurally generated via a custom Blender MCP socket bridge (blender_mcp_addon.py, blender_mcp_bridge.py, generate_reactor_final.py).

The Rust core couples four physical solvers inside SodiumFastReactor (rust/src/reactor.rs) at $\Delta t = 10\,\text{ms}$ (0.01 s):

  1. Fast-Spectrum Monte Carlo Neutron Transport (rust/src/neutronics.rs):
  2. Tracks 3D phase-space Neutron particles (position: Vector3<f64>, direction: UnitVector3<f64>, energy: f64 in eV, weight, generation) born from a Pu-239 Watt fission spectrum (sample_watt_spectrum), stepping across 10-group ENDF/B-VIII.0 fast cross-sections (CrossSections: $\sigma_f, \sigma_c, \sigma_s, \nu$) with power iteration to update $k_{\text{eff}}$.
  3. Six-Group Pu-239 Delayed-Neutron Point Kinetics (rust/src/kinetics.rs):
  4. Integrates the coupled stiff point-kinetics ODEs for normalized neutron population $N(t)$ and the 6 delayed-neutron precursor groups $\vec{C}(t) \in \mathbb{R}^6$ (nalgebra::Vector6<f64>) using Pu-239 fast-spectrum parameters ($\beta = 0.0020$, $\Lambda = 1.0 \times 10^{-7}\,\text{s}$, $\vec{\lambda} = [0.0127, 0.0317, 0.115, 0.311, 1.40, 3.87]\,\text{s}^{-1}$, $\vec{\beta}_{\text{frac}} = [0.038, 0.213, 0.188, 0.407, 0.128, 0.026]$): $$\frac{dN}{dt} = \frac{\rho(t) - \beta}{\Lambda} N(t) + \sum_{i=1}^6 \lambda_i C_i(t), \qquad \frac{dC_i}{dt} = \frac{\beta_i}{\Lambda} N(t) - \lambda_i C_i(t)$$
  5. Total reactivity $\rho(t)$ sums 9 control-rod bank worth curves, fuel Doppler feedback, and sodium coolant expansion feedback, triggering automatic warnings at $T_{\text{coolant}} > 550^\circ\text{C}$, $\rho > \$0.50$, or prompt criticality ($\rho \ge \beta$, i.e. $\$1.00$).
  6. 1D Axial Liquid-Sodium Thermal Hydraulics (rust/src/thermal_hydraulics.rs):
  7. Models num_channels = 57 assemblies, each a 20-node axial CoolantChannel with num_pins = 271 fuel pins of diameter $D_{\text{pin}} = 8.5\,\text{mm}$ on a triangular pitch $P = 10.5\,\text{mm}$, interstitial flow area $A_{\text{flow}} = N_{\text{pins}} \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P^2 - \frac{\pi}{4} D_{\text{pin}}^2\right)$, hydraulic diameter $D_h = 4 A_{\text{flow}} / (\pi D_{\text{pin}} N_{\text{pins}})$, temperature-dependent SodiumProperties ($\rho(T), c_p(T), k(T), \mu(T), \text{Pr}(T)$), cosine axial power peaking, and convective heat transfer coefficients (heat_transfer_coefficient).
  8. 2 GWh Two-Tank Molten Salt Thermal Storage (rust/src/storage.rs):
  9. Models solar salt ($60\%\,\text{NaNO}_3 / 40\%\,\text{KNO}_3$, melting point $238^\circ\text{C}$, $\rho(T) = 2263.0 - 0.488(T - 273.15)\,\text{kg/m}^3$, $c_p = 1520\,\text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$, Arrhenius viscosity $\mu(T) = 2.414 \times 10^{-5} \exp(422.0 / (T_C - 144.0))\,\text{Pa}\cdot\text{s}$) across a $700^\circ\text{C}$ (973 K) hot_tank and $300^\circ\text{C}$ (573 K) cold_tank with ambient heat loss, decoupling reactor thermal power from peaking grid electricity demand.

5.2 buckeye: Fast-Spectrum Criticality, 2-Group Diffusion, 2D FVM & GPU Raymarched Neutronics

Repository: /Users/ember/dev/buckeye (5 commits on 2025-12-31 through 43effdb).

buckeye is a two-part nuclear physics and GPU visualization suite investigating fast-spectrum supercritical assemblies (Pu-239 Jezebel benchmark PU-MET-FAST-001 and U-235/U-238 systems), coupled neutronics-hydrodynamics (Bethe-Feynman yield / fizzle dynamics based on arXiv:1606.01670v1), and time-dependent GPU Monte Carlo raymarching:

  1. Single-Group & Two-Group ENDF/B-VIII.0 Neutronics (nuclear_physics.py, two_group_physics.py, spatial_neutronics.py, coupled_physics.py):
  2. two_group_physics.py partitions the fast spectrum at $1\,\text{MeV}$ (the U-238 fast-fission threshold) with Watt fission birth fractions $\chi_1 = 0.75$ ($E > 1\,\text{MeV}$, $E_{\text{avg}} = 2.0\,\text{MeV}$) and $\chi_2 = 0.25$ ($0.1\,\text{eV} < E < 1\,\text{MeV}$, $E_{\text{avg}} = 0.4\,\text{MeV}$) and down-scattering $\sigma_{s,1\to 2} = 0.12\,\text{b}$ (PU239_TWO_GROUP) and $0.18\,\text{b}$ (U238_TWO_GROUP).
  3. spatial_neutronics.py implements a 2nd-order conservative Finite Volume Method (FVM) solver on a 2D cylindrical $(r, z)$ mesh (CylindricalMesh) using scipy.sparse eigenvalue solvers (eigs/eigsh) to compute spatial eigenmodes and $k_{\text{eff}}$ across spherical, cylindrical, and prolate/oblate ("football") geometries (geometry_comparison.png).
  4. Rigorous Self-Audit of Transport & EOS Physics (PHYSICS_REVIEW.md):
  5. In PHYSICS_REVIEW.md, Ember conducted a line-by-line mathematical audit of the initial diffusion and hydrodynamics code, documenting and fixing eight transport and thermodynamic errors:
  6. Replacing a naive fission-only lifetime formula with the true multiplying-medium prompt generation time $\Lambda = \frac{1}{v \Sigma_a k_{\text{eff}}}$ and Rossi alpha $\alpha = \frac{k_{\text{eff}} - 1}{\Lambda} = v \Sigma_a (k_{\text{eff}} - 1)$.
  7. Replacing the pure-scattering Milne extrapolation length $\delta = 0.7104 \lambda_{\text{tr}}$ (valid only for secondary-neutron number $c = 1$) with the Case & Zweifel Mark transport approximation for absorbing media: $$\frac{\delta}{\lambda_{\text{tr}}} = 0.7104 \sqrt{3} \sqrt{\frac{c}{1 + \frac{5}{3}c}}$$
  8. Replacing $k_\infty = \nu \Sigma_f / \Sigma_a$ in the pre-initiation fizzle model (advanced_simulations.py) with the leakage-corrected effective multiplication factor $k_{\text{eff}} = \frac{k_\infty}{1 + L^2 B_g^2}$.
  9. Augmenting the high-compression Equation of State (ideal gas + $\frac{1}{3} a T^4$ radiation pressure) with Fermi electron degeneracy pressure $P_{\text{deg}} = K (\rho/\mu_e)^{5/3}$ (which reaches $\sim 10^{12}\,\text{Pa}$ at $3\times$ Pu compression), yielding validated supercritical disassembly outputs ($6.2\,\text{kg}$ Pu-239 at $c = 2.5$ compression $\to 44.88\,\text{kt}$ yield, peak $T = 1.71 \times 10^8\,\text{K}$, peak $P = 2207\,\text{Gbar}$, Rossi $\alpha = 5.15 \times 10^8\,\text{s}^{-1}$).
  10. wgpu Compute Monte Carlo & Volumetric/Trail Raymarching (gpu/runner/src/main.rs, gpu/runner/src/time_sim.rs, gpu/runner/src/shader.wgsl):
  11. TimeSimulator (time_sim.rs) runs a time-stepped GPU compute pipeline (simulate.wgsl) over 5,000 initial neutrons across 600 time steps and up to 50,000 atomic collision events (CollisionEvent with event_type: 1 = elastic in cyan-blue, 2 = fission in white-gold, 3 = capture in red, 4 = escape in gray).
  12. TrailRenderer (trail_renderer.rs and shader.wgsl) renders 1080p60/30fps frames (gpu/runner/time_*.png, trail_*.png) combining 3D texture volumetric raymarching (volume_texture: texture_3d<f32>) with analytical ray-sphere glow intersection (ray_sphere_intersect) across spherical (geometry_type == 0u) and prolate football (geometry_type == 1u) assemblies.
